entries.description:
A heavily sampled song for cave, underground, factory, etc. The port is based on a MIDI sequenced by DORKAS.



Note that due to the size of samples, some of vanilla samples for misc song or SFX had to be sacrificed. There are two versions for this, namely "no level clear" and "no p-switch". "No level clear" doesn't include the sample used by the level clear song so when the level has a goal tape, you should avoid using this (otherwise it will sound strange). "No p-switch" is similar to that.

Also note that both versions don't have the sample of explosion which is used by a lightning or blargg.

entries.description:
In early 2010, during the development of Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode I, legendary Sonic game composer Jun Senoue was toiling away in his office, trying to think of a song that would fit well with a difficult, climactic final boss. He thought to himself, "This boss is very hard and there is a lot at stake. It needs to be an epic song of just the right length to fit with the game's final fight against Eggman."



So he began composing a new song. After months of hard work, thinking of a good melody to use for the song, thinking of the right instruments to use, thinking and thinking, working and working, he finally finished it - his ultimate masterpiece, E.G.G. Station Zone. An amazingly in-depth composition that not even the likes of Yoko Shimomura or Koji Kondo would ever have any hopes of beating out in terms of sheer creativity and epic-ness. Other video game composers since then have looked upon themselves in shame, knowing that they will never match the quality of this critically-acclaimed song.



And that is where I come in. Using the limitations of the sound engine used by Super Mario World, I have recreated this song using only the original game's instruments in the best way I could.



Do not the song duration above fool you. This is actually super long and one of the most amazing, epic songs you will ever hear in your life. It masters the art of knowing how not to be repetitive or anticlimactic in any way possible. It is a must-have for your SMW hacks. This song can easily fit in any final boss scenario, to give it the climactic, game-finale feeling it deserves. Jun Senoue's finest work is finally available for you to use, and I am pleased to have brought this masterpiece to your ROM hacks.
entries.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode I - E.G.G. Station Zone

entries.description:
The second cutscene theme from Puyo Puyo, also present in Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine as a remix for Stage 13 (A.K.A Robotnik's stage)'s intro, and a version more faithful to the original which has gone unused (Sad!). It was also used in the Mega Drive version of Madou Monogatari as its second opening theme, tho I'm not sure about the other versions of that game.



Anyway, this song would definitely fit well with a dramatic and final cutscene, so if y'all want to use this for a hack, definitely consider that as a option. If not, the final levels of your hack would also benefit from that. Or you can just ignore this and use it on your own way, I dont care LOL



Oh, and btw, thank JonKaruzu for helping out with the last parts of the conversion of the original SPC to MML. While my skills with MML have definitely been getting better, I'm still not very comfortable with it, so help like this is always very appreciated >:]

entries.description:
The Credits theme from Columns III, AFAIK only heard if you beat the game on Hard Mode, but what do I know, I ain't a expert on this game, I only know it has some damn good music lol



You'll probably remember this from Sonic Megamix's Misty Maze Zone tho, a pretty competent Sonic hack that pretty much made my (and many others's) childhood, and it's the main reason why I did this lmao. This could be either used like in the original game, as a credits theme, or this could also be used like in Sonic Megamix, as a water level theme. You have to decide on this one LOL



This one, with the power of FM Sampling, also uses most of the original samples from Columns III, but it also uses noise at some parts and it isn't totally accurate (mostly due to the MIDI I used), but it's still accurate enough I guess ¯\_(ツ)_/¯



Update: Mostly fixed a few minor stuff Maxo told me about, and now not only is most of the problems solved, it's actually closer to the original song now (hopefully the brass doesn't end TOO early tho), so that's good



Update 2 (hopefully this is the last one tho): Changed the bass and snare to something that doesn't have noise tacked on into those, and while the snare isn't as good as the original one, at least it's noise-free lmao



oh, and I also accurately tuned the bass, so yeah lol
entries.name: Columns III: Revenge of Columns - Column Dive

The very happy theme for the Grass Land Map of Kirby's Dream Land 3. Like the game, this would best be suited in grassy overworlds, or first overworlds in general (unless you start in hell or any other place that isn't supposed to be a happy first overworld, in which case I don't recommend using this port for those purposes at all LMAO)



This also tries to be at least accurate enough to the original that there isn't many noticeable differences to it and the original, and this is technically one of the first ports that I actually give a damn about accuracy too. Well, enjoy it I guess



(also when is Ultima gonna stop flooding the waiting section with ports, amirite 👀)



Update: musicalman helped me with a few stuff, and now this port should be more true to the original. Once again, enjoy lmao

entries.description:
This is a SNES arrangement of Team Rainbow Rocket's battle theme from Pokemon USUM, where the original was basically a remix of the original Team Rocket battle theme from Pokemon G/S/C (was also present in Pokemon HGSS).



This was VERY hard to do honestly; 3-4 days were spent just to make the samples and fit everything in the MIDI I used to fit the SNES's 8-channel limit, and then another 3-4 days to optimize and sequence this MML. I'm surprised this has worked so well tho, considering the sheer amount of samples and MML size that this port has, and the MIDI also had 13 channels, so it was kind of a wonder how it was possible to fit in everything (as you can see by how busy this port is); guess this is the true power of making chord samples lol



This could be used for a long boss fight, or a long chase sequence, but other than that, I dunno if this has many uses; and again, this port is really large, so use this with caution.



oh yeah, MIDI is by ShinkoNetCavy btw



Update: Fixed the tuning of the distorted guitar, and (hopefully) improved the mixing a bit.
entries.name: Pokémon Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon - Battle! Team Rainbow Rocket (SNES Arrange)

entries.description:
posting a Tyrian port in place of worldpeace because why not



This is A Field For Mag from the PC only game Tyrian, one of the very few non-Japanese OPL/AdLib games which used it's chip in the best possible way, same with the MIDI version of that same game, but it's not nearly as impressive as what it achieved with the OPL2 chip, sorry lmao.



Anyway, this is a very final-like song, so the only best way to use this is for a final level or just using it for the final stages of your hack. Tho it could also work for a early level or even a cutscene probably; maybe a space level too, again, as long as it's final enough or it just fits your hack's atmosphere enough, this could be a very good port for that purpose lol



Update: Fixed the SFX problem, and added a bit of new instrumentation to the port.
entries.name: Tyrian - A Field For Mag (Arrangement)

Thanks to a friend, I have managed to acquire every single sample from the Past songs in Sonic CD, and well, since I had them, I decided to do something similar to Izuna's port of Stardust Speedway Past, where I tried to make this as accurate to the original as possible, but of course there might be a few problems, so I still need feedback to make this as accurate as it can get lol



Oh yeah, use this if you need a theme for a funky and upbeat factory or castle, or for something else that you may think up because I can't think of any other example this theme would fit; sorry lol



Btw, thanks to The Boys and Girls™ for helping me with this port ;)

preeeeeetty sure y'all were expecting me to do this at some point huh



fine then, have your goddamn hues you sick fucks



uhh, I mean



This is the more overrated version of Stardust Speedway Bad Future, A.K.A the JP version. This could fit in quite a few funky situations, like a chase scene, a castle, a highway, a boss battle, a night level, and probably even more shit that I don't know about right now!
entries.name: Sonic CD (JP/EU) - Stardust Speedway Zone (Bad Future)

entries.description: One of the Competition Mode track themes from S3&K, this would best suit a carnival or bonus level.
entries.name: Sonic 3 & Knuckles - Balloon Park

entries.description:
This song originates from a ship in Chrono Cross; the S.S. Invincible, or Zelbess, which is a cruise ship that has some attractions like a casino. So use this for a level that gives the player vibes of fun and relaxation.



Requester: Roadhog360 Gaming

MIDI credit: Dermot Mac Flannchaidh



(EDIT: Changed the drumbeat before the song loops.)
entries.name: Chrono Cross - Zelbess

entries.description:
This is the Egypt stage theme from DuckTales 2.

Could fit pyramids or temples.
entries.name: DuckTales 2 - Egypt

entries.description:
This is Palmtree Panic Bad Future, and also the first port that I made where it's actually from (Naofumi) Hataya and not (Masafumi) Ogata this time around (tho I mean, I have technically already did one or two Ogata tracks from each stage that he composed for Sonic CD, so I think this is the perfect time to give Hataya a chance lol)



This port is actually better suited for a factory or something similar surprisingly, or you can go the same way as the original did and use this for a mechanical forest level; either way, it's on you ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
entries.name: Sonic CD (JP/EU) - Palmtree Panic Zone (Bad Future)

entries.description: The strong song from the Sabrewulf in Killer Instinct. Great for your Castle Theme.
entries.name: Killer Instinct - Sabrewulf Theme

entries.description:
(Also known as "Bomb Ring")



The song that plays in Ring of Bomb in Final Fantasy IV.
entries.name: Final Fantasy IV - Bomb Ring

entries.description: The upbeat and tense tune to the first level in the 8-bit Sonic 2, Underground Zone. This is probably more appropriate for a fast-paced late-game mountain level than a first level, though.
entries.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 (MS/GG) - Underground Zone

entries.description:
The happy song played on the beach track in Mario Kart Super Circuit. Would obviously suit a beach level.



EDIT: Fixed the syncing on #6.
entries.name: Mario Kart: Super Circuit - Shy Guy Beach

entries.description: Melancholic song that plays during the downtime of some colossus fights.
entries.name: Shadow of the Colossus - Silence

entries.description: Unsampled version of Twoson from Earthbound. Good for towns.
entries.name: EarthBound - Twoson

entries.description:
This is the Mu Stage theme from DuckTales 2.

Fits perfectly for beach levels.
entries.name: DuckTales 2 - Mu

entries.description: The song you hear when you fight a boss in Dragon Ball Z - Attack of the Saiyans. It can be used for boss battles really well.
entries.name: Dragon Ball Z - Attack of the Saiyans - Raditz/Nappa Boss Battle

entries.description: Music played at the bonus level of the game. Can fit small bonus rooms and so on.
entries.name: M.C Kids - Bonus theme

entries.description:
Song played in the jungle regions of Jurassic Park. It's not recommended to use this song in a level that'll utilize the "Hurry Up" flag as it messes up the percussion loop.



Please give credit if used.
entries.name: Jurassic Park - Raptor Rap

entries.description:
Song played in the mountain regions of Jurassic Park. It's not recommended to use this song in a level that'll utilize the "Hurry Up" flag as it messes up the percussion loop.



Please give credit if used.
entries.name: Jurassic Park - Triceratops Trot

entries.description: Intense song suitable for intense areas.
entries.name: Hyper Duel (Arcade) - Over Drive / Full Burner

entries.description:
A theme from the Ace Attorney series that makes the player think out of the box.



There's two variants of this song in the download. One of them is the standard port, which can fit a cut scene, or mini-game. The other one is an optimized version so that it can be used globally for a P-Switch theme.
entries.name: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Justice for All - Magic and Tricks

entries.description:
Theme that plays in stage 6 of Castlevania Chronicles. It's string-filled and fits castles really well. Works for other sorts of dangerous environments too.



Requester: StrikeForcer



(FIXES: The lead section is entirely changed with better instruments and volume changes. Replaced the extra instrument that was in the previous version since it wasn't in the official version of the song. Fixed a few incorrect notes.)
entries.name: Castlevania Chronicles - The Tower of Dolls

entries.description:
This is a fairly simple and quick unsampled port of the original Rainbow Road theme from Super Mario Kart, a theme which has spawned countless iterations of it for all the other Mario Kart games after this one. If it's actually good tho, well, I'll let you decide lol



It's best usage would definitely be in a extra world level a la Star Road from the original SMW, but this could be used in space levels in general I guess.



Update: Tried to properly emulate the drum pitch changes this time around, and also removed the pitch modulation since it was kinda useless lol
entries.name: Super Mario Kart - Rainbow Road

entries.description:
An insane upbeat cap theme from Super Mario 64. This will fit for starman or some fast athletic cavern level.



Lower or remove the echo delay if you're going to use it for starman.
entries.name: Super Mario 64 - Metallic Mario

entries.description:
A very calm, ambient, and atmospheric song from DC2's bramble levels.



Please give credit if used.
entries.name: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest - Stickerbush Symphony

entries.description: this theme fits into many types of levels but gets better at bonus levels
entries.name: Stunt Race FX - King's Forest

entries.description:
This is a fast-paced song from Star Fox. It's epic, and that's what makes it well-known. The best use of this song I can think of is for space levels, but it can be used for intense/special levels as well.



MIDI Credit: King Meteor
entries.name: Star Fox - Corneria

entries.description:
Theme for the first few maps of Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones. Suitable for grassland levels.



The MML file is cross-compiled from a different MML dialect using a custom Lua script, and then manually optimized.
entries.name: Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones - Distant Roads

entries.description: This is a short, but dizzyingly intense song from SMG (I love music like this btw). This was for a long time on my 'impossible ports that I will eventually try anyway' list. It helped relieve some stress at any rate, and it turned out decent enough.
entries.name: Super Mario Galaxy - The Big Staircase

entries.description:
A 16-bit remix of the frantic, albeit repetitive song that plays during the battle in Wily stage from the first Mega Man game.



Special thank goes to Wakana for help me fixing this port.
entries.name: Mega Man - Wily Stage Boss (16-bit arrangement)

entries.description: This is an atmospheric and ominous song with a space and/or night time feel. It could work well for sky/space overworld sections, Yoshi houses (or other "rest" areas), water levels, dark/night level, or anything with a space vibe. Probably not very fitting for anything fast paced.
entries.name: The 7th Saga - The Farthest Reaches

entries.description: Neutopia II grassland & forest zone theme. I think it is useful grassland & forest stage.
entries.name: Neutopia II - Sphere 1

entries.description:
One of the better songs from this particular Pokémon game. It sounds mildly dramatic and chill. This can probably work in a mechanical level, like a factory. Might even work as a water level theme because of the slow pace of the song. Really anything "indoorsy" will do. 



EXTRA NOTE: This is exactly how it was in Idol 9 round 2, except I swapped channels so that the SFX doesn't interrupt the song too much.
entries.name: Pokémon X/Y - Kalos Power Plant

entries.description:
This is a very slow and relaxing theme from Stardew Valley. It sounds "cold". In the game, it plays during the winter season, so I'd probably use this port for an area just as similar.



EXTRA NOTES: This is exactly how it was in Idol 9 round 3. I should mention that this port does NOT loop. It just ends, like the original SMW credits theme.
entries.name: Stardew Valley - The Wind Can Be Still

entries.description:
Also known as: Mario Forever - Apoplexy Tanks



The intense tank theme that plays during the tank levels on World 8 of Mario Forever. Can be used for penultimate or final levels. It can also be suited for factories, fire levels or whatever could suit it.



UPDATE:

Now made the song more closer to the original, and it now includes 3 other versions of the song, one that loops properly, one with better panning (no more Amiga hardpanning) and one that has both proper looping and panning. You may want the latter for the best sounding version.
entries.name: Bee Hunter - Apoplexy

entries.description:
The obscure-ass Stage 1 theme from this obscure-ass arkanoid/eroge hybrid title from the 80s/90s or whatever called Cyberblock Metal Orange. Also sounds very Japanese and space like, so this would certainly fit in either a combination of both levels (I'd legit want to see a level which has a Japanese shrine in space playing this btw) or just space-y levels in general. Not much else, tho



Update: Now much better made and even more Sakimoto like! (hopefully).
entries.name: Cyberblock Metal Orange - Stage 1

entries.description: Port of Illusion from F-Zero Climax. Could fit intense levels, bosses and chase sequences.
entries.name: F-Zero Climax - Illusion

entries.description: This is Gimmick (A.K.A Mr.Gimmick)'s intro theme. Since it doesn't loop, the only way this would fit is in intro screens, so be careful. This is a sampled version with Kirby and Earthbound samples btw
entries.name: Gimmick! - Good Morning

entries.description: This is Gimmick (A.K.A Mr.Gimmick)'s intro theme. Since it doesn't loop, the only way this would fit is in intro screens, so be careful. This is a unsampled version btw
entries.name: Gimmick! - Good Morning

entries.description:
This is the song that plays for Military Sora in 100% Orange Juice. It can fit in variety of levels.







Credit to pieordie1 for the MIDI in VGMusic website.



(Chords and Drum has been edited in terms of position)
entries.name: 100% Orange Juice - Military Sora's Theme

entries.description: This is a arranged version of Milky Way Wishes from Kirby Super Star. Could fit title themes, but could also fit a overworld, specifically one that could be related to space.
entries.name: Kirby Super Star - Milky Way Wishes (Arranged)

entries.description: This is an arranged version of Way of the Fighting King from Kirby Super Star. Could fit title themes, but could also fit final and medieval overworlds.
entries.name: Kirby Super Star - Way of the Fighting King (Arranged)

entries.description:
This is a Megaman X1 styled arrangement of the Mr. X Castle theme from Megaman 6. Could fit final levels very well.



Thanks to YuzuMSX for helping me with making this more accurate to X1's style btw
entries.name: Mega Man 6 - Mr. X's Castle (X1 Style)

entries.description: This is a Kyuuyaku Megami Tensei styled arrangement of Shovel Knight's Iron Whale stage theme. Fits water levels.
entries.name: Shovel Knight - A Thousand Leagues Below (KMT Styled)

entries.description:
Requested by StrikeForcer. (tho I already wanted to do this song for a while ago lol)



The less famous, but still pretty kickass tune for the US version of Sonic CD's Stardust Speedway Bad Future levels. Mostly used for space levels, but could also be used for night levels and other stuff, I dunno.



Update: Fixed the guitar and bass, added a few new stuff to make this sound fuller, and removed the need of a sample group.



Update 2: Wakana gave me a new muted guitar sample for this port, and he told me there were some desyncs on #4, so i (hopefully) fixed that too lol
entries.name: Sonic CD (US) - Stardust Speedway Zone (Bad Future)

entries.description: from the SNES "AHH Real Monsters" game this is a short,looped piece that's kind of spooky. It would work well for sections in a ghost house or other area haunted areas. It would probably sound best in shorter sections and not as the song for a long/entire level as it's some what short.
entries.name: AHH Real Monsters - Stage Intro 1

entries.description: you know I had to do it to em
entries.name: Luis Fonsi - Despacito

entries.description:
The wonderful battle song you hear when fighting count Cannoli in WMoD. Can fit mid-bosses, since it's kind of repetitive and short, yet memorable.

Watch out with noise SFX in your levels, since the song uses noise.
entries.name: Wario: Master of Disguise - Count Cannoli Battle

entries.description: The space song everyone loves. This is kind of repetitive, especially in the second half, thus I suggest it for short levels in general. Theme-wise, obviously, it fits any level where Mario flies trough the level.
entries.name: Bag Raiders - Shooting Stars

entries.description: Also known as my dad's theme. This theme would greatly suit a battle against someone which has a mysterious personality, such as dad Saint Germain from CoD, which is a time traveler.
entries.name: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness - The Visitor in the Silk Hat

entries.description:
Would fit in a beach level, obviously.

(Yes, these are Mario Kart DS samples.)
entries.name: Cool Beach Song

entries.description: The upbeat song that plays in Act 2 of Hydrocity Zone. This port doesn't really sound very "Genesis", but I think it still sounds nice by its own merits. I ended up using only samples from Tetris Attack... as well as its echo parameters, sue me.
entries.name: Sonic 3 & Knuckles - Hydrocity Zone Act 2

entries.description: Frog Legs Dancing With A Little Salt
entries.name: Kero Blaster - Checkin' Out

entries.description: The first Stage of Gradius 2 arranged using Gradius 3 samples.
entries.name: Gradius II - Burning Heat

entries.description: This is a short calm song from Treasure Hunter G. I've wanted to port this one for a while. I didn't rip samples from the game; I decided to aim for a spacious feel in my samples while still being faithful to the original instrumentation. Overall I think it has the lush sound I strive for when porting music of this style.
entries.name: Treasure Hunter G - Surrounded by Forest 2

entries.description: This is a short calm song from Treasure Hunter G. I've wanted to port this one for a while. This port was made to match my sampled version as closely as I could, and might sound a little more fitting in hacks.
entries.name: Treasure Hunter G - Surrounded by Forest 2

entries.description:
16-bit version of the lively Pokémon Gold music. 

It can be used on animated levels, like cities, calm fields, or perhaps on happy maps.
entries.name: Pokémon FireRed/LeafGreen - Four Island / Five Island

entries.description:
This is the theme that plays in Dimble Wood, the forest with the walking trees... and the Carrot minigame.



Original song by Yoko Shimomura.



Arranged by me.
entries.name: Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story - Let's Meet in the Mysterious Forest

entries.description: This is the quiet song of the national park of the game "Pokémon G/S/C". Can be used on quiet levels, such as fields, happy forests etc.
entries.name: Pokémon Gold/Silver/Crystal - National Park (16-bit remix)

entries.description: An old custom composition I originally used for a rainy beach level. Good for rainy/cloudy beaches (or maybe not only beaches, who knows).
entries.name: Cloudy Beach

entries.description: Remember those annoying sunken ship levels from Donkey Kong Country 2 that you had to swim through? Well then, surely you've heard this theme then. This fits what you'd expect it to fit; levels that look like sunken ships.
entries.name: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest - Lockjaw's Saga

entries.description:
This is the battle theme from the first Battle Network, just like what you seen in Idol 9's first round. I wasn't planning on releasing any Idol ports of mine, but since this was already optimized, I said "hey, why not", and decided to release this lol. IMO, this theme is a pretty good theme for friendly battles and races, and this theme would be best suited for those, but it could also fit athletic levels quite well. Maybe.



Fun fact btw: some people were talking about why I used SMW samples for the drums, and that's actually because I misinterpreted the challenge and I didn't know you could use more than 3 samples (else I would've used some sweet TR-909 drums >.>); at least I didn't get DQed because of it tho, so that's good
entries.name: Mega Man Battle Network - Operation!

entries.description:
A theme from the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon Series. Despite the title, this song doesn't really sound like a cave theme at all (at least for SMW levels). This theme is a nice tune that is more fitting for mountainous environments, grasslands, and sometimes deserts.



UPDATES: Replaced the nylon guitar for a steel guitar. Added more instrumentation to the beginning. Increased the echo reverb and delay. Various volume and panning changes.
entries.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gates to Infinity - Stony Cave

entries.description: This is Megaman Battle Chip Challenge's battle theme, which IMO is one of the best battle themes in the entire Battle Network series (too bad the game doesn't have any more memorable tunes tho, outside of maybe the boss theme; the gameplay is a bit boring too, but it's still pretty fast paced, which I like). This could be used both for intense levels and friendly boss battles, which is a pretty nice middle ground if you ask me lol
entries.name: Mega Man Battle Chip Challenge - Navi Clash! (Battle Theme)

entries.description: For another BCC port, here's the title screen theme of this game; it's a pretty epic one and it doesn't loop at all (since it has a proper ending, and it would sound weird if looped), so only use this for short intros and title sequences for hacks that need a more epic and adventurous vibe. Sadly tho there's not many other uses for this lol
entries.name: Mega Man Battle Chip Challenge - Title Screen

entries.description: This song has an intro and about a 35 second loop. It's upbeat and relatively smooth, for a TMNT song. Little down time make this a good song for levels that have a constant pace, would also work great in Switch Palaces and Bonus Levels. Enjoy!
entries.name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles IV: Turtles in Time - Neon Night Riders

entries.description:
This is the theme that plays in Temporal Tower, which is the final dungeon of PMD: EoT/D/S (well, if you don't count the post-game dungeons that is). This may be a very iconic tune for the people who played this game, and IMO it's definitely one of the best tunes in the entirety of the PMD franchise due to that. 



Because of the final level vibes this has, this should only be used in a final level, especially in a climactic final level before the final boss. This would also be better suited for hacks with a heavier story IMO, but yeah, this still boils down to what and how you want to use this, I'm just a simple porter after all lol
entries.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time/Darkness/Sky - Temporal Tower

entries.description:
A very calm, relaxing song that would fit a forest or nighttime atmosphere well.



You may need to lower echo delay to make this work for you, as it cuts pretty close. It also removes samples required for Yoshi and Blargg SFX, so you can't use either of those in a level with this song (not that you'd have Blarggs in this kind of setting anyway, but you never know...). Credit to Pinci for the piano samples.



(also if anyone knows if there's an official name for this song please let me know!)
entries.name: DS Nishimura Kyotaro Suspense - Track 0015

entries.description:
Song for boss fights. Very short, don't use it on long epic boss fights. I added a bunch of chords and drums to make it sound nicer.



Original:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-aIfP9cLwd0
entries.name: KiKi KaiKai - Boss Fight

entries.description: It gets good in deserts.
entries.name: Terranigma - Nomads In a Desert

entries.description: This is a sports/hype themed track that repeats as variations on a melody line with a strong back beat and percussion samples.This could work well in a switch palace, bonus area, or VVVVVV style level.
entries.name: NBA Give 'N Go - Game BGM 6

entries.description: A fast-paced intense song from the 3d Ultra Pinball Creep night PC game. It's probably most useful for chases, but could likely be useful for epic fights as well. Unfortunately I don't have track names for this game, or else I would've used those instead of a track number.
entries.name: 3D Ultra Pinball: Creep Night - Track 28

entries.description:
This is a recreation of the main menu theme from Harry Potter: Chamber of Secrets for the Game Boy Advance.



The GBA version's music is almost identical to the GBC version's, despite being different in gameplay. The only difference is that the bass instrument is more realistic, the noise channel of the original Game Boy is no longer used, and the pulse waves are messed up.
entries.name: Harry Potter: Chamber of Secrets (GBA) - Main Menu

entries.description: A beautiful waltz from Illusion of Gaia that would be great for cloud levels or towns
entries.name: Illusion of Gaia - Lively City

entries.description: This composition is a cheery tune that is intended to fit for a sky-styled overworld, but it could definitely work for a large generic overworld too.
entries.name: Floating Overworld

entries.description:
This is Team Dark's theme song from Sonic Heroes, which was requested by StrikeForcer. When he first asked me to do this song, I wasn't too into the idea back then, and back then I also found it to be too complicated to be done. However, I slowly got more and more interested in this song, and honestly it actually wasn't as hard as I thought, mostly due to all the recent techniques I've learned that helped a lot here, especially chord sampling. Well, I hope you like this I guess (even if you wanted a unsampled version instead) :P



Anyway, due to the way the song is structured, I think the best way to use this is for a long and badass intro sequence, or if you want it for something more plausible, a badass ending sequence. However, since it's looped, you could use this for a level as well; I mean, why not, it's your hack after all lol



Oh, and another thing: this song is preeeeeeetty big, mostly due to the fact this song is literally 3 minutes long, so if you need more space for something else, think about it before you use this. That's all lmao
entries.name: Sonic Heroes - This Machine (Team Dark's Theme)

entries.description:
The funky theme from Zaxxon's Motherbase 2000, as seen in Idol Round 5. This hasn't really been recieved that well in Idol, but honestly the main problem when I submitted this to it seemed to be about the song choice, and rarely about the port itself, so I think this should be fine to submit.



Anyway, I'd say this should fit urban, night and space zones quite well, but honestly I'm not too sure myself. Just use this in a way you feel comfortable I guess lol



EDIT: Added a optimized and a unoptimized version; use the optimized version if you want to insert this into a hack, because it removes a lot of the space this would have (tho it doesn't change much of the song); the unoptimized version is just for listening lol
entries.name: Zaxxon's Motherbase 2000 - Stage 2 (Part 1)

entries.description: Could fit with beach theme
entries.name: WHITE ALBUM 2 - Sunshine Day

entries.description:
This is the Cingular tune that used to be on old AT&T phones. Original author unknown.



If you want to use it as global, in the AMK music list, put the global song it will replace into the locals with its number intact and then replace that.
entries.name: Cingular Tune

entries.description:
The jungle theme from the NES port of Metal Gear. Original by Kazuki Muraoka.



Not only is the jungle level exclusive to the NES version, this game's soundtrack is different from the MSX version. And I don't mean that they sound different as in what happens when a song is transferred from one sound chip to another. I mean different as in the compositions are different. Only half of the songs from the MSX version are the same as in the NES version.
entries.name: Metal Gear (NES) - Jungle

entries.description:
This is SearchMan.EXE's theme from Megaman Battle Network 4.5 Real Operation, which was only released on Japan. It's a jazzy/downtempo arrangement of the theme of his Robot Master counterpart, which first appeared in Megaman 8 and was composed by Shuusaku Uchiyama; this arrangement was Akari Kaida's doing tho if I'm not mistaken, but aaaaany way... 



This would be best suited for cutscenes or overworlds due to it's short length, like a sky, space or grassland overworld. It's probably not suited for a level tho, unless it's in a bonus room, which this would probably fit best, I dunno lol



Update: Changed the kick to a kick sample from Der Langrisser, and also credited Shuusaku Uchiyama on the SPC too because why not lmao
entries.name: Rockman EXE 4.5: Real Operation - Theme of SearchMan

entries.description:
This is the regular boss theme from Lufia 2: Rise of the Sinistrals.



My thanks to LadiesMan217 for help with the cymbals and volume balancing.
entries.name: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals - Battle #2

entries.description: This is an almost-perfect port of Beldoroon's (now named Dubmood) 'If We Go Underwater'. This song was not originally from a game, but despite that, was still originally an Amiga .mod file.
entries.name: Dubmood - If We Go Underwater

entries.description:
This song plays during the Fantasy Knight transformation in Ape Escape 3. It's a repetitive, yet catchy tune. It's fairly short, so it's probably not a good idea to use it in long levels. I'd say it's best suited for an overworld, bonus room, or cut scene. 



Requester: SomeGuy712x
entries.name: Ape Escape 3 - Fantasy Knight

entries.description: This is a dark and spooky track that can be a fairly versatile track as there is no imposing lead/melody line. It could work well as music for any level that fits it's theme, but will feel at home in slow to medium paced levels, or levels with platforming but not at a high rate of speed. Might also work well for a puzzle level.
entries.name: Jelly Boy - Fire Pits

entries.description:
This upbeat song is from two games: 



Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time & Darkness

Pokémon Super Mystery Dungeon



This song works well when used in any indoor level. A castle, cave, ghost house, etc. (probably NOT for a switch palace)



UPDATE: Tacked on $F4 $02 to make the entire thing sound much better than before. I also changed a few things here and there a while back, but can't remember what exactly (it was probably ADSR or something).
entries.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time/Darkness/Sky - Amp Plains

entries.description:
A very chill theme from Sonic Mania. It plays in the 2nd act of the Press Garden Zone. Definitely fitting for ice levels, mountains, and perhaps fortresses. I wouldn't recommend this theme for an underground level.



EDITS: Lowered master volume from 237 → 216. Pitch bends are more accurate. Echo of bass/low kick were removed. Increased echo feedback a little bit. Organ is now tuned properly



UPDATES: Tacked on $F4 $02 to make it sound better. Removed the panning on the @14. Raised volumes of kicks, claps, and the organ. Adjusted the @0 ADSR.
entries.name: Sonic Mania - Blossom Haze (Press Garden Zone Act 2)

entries.description:
A very "ruinsy" sounding theme from LOZ: Minish Cap. This theme works for castles/fortresses. It fits a ghost house (although it's not haunted), and it sort of fits an airship.



UPDATE: Tacked on $F4 $02 to make it sound better.
entries.name: The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap - Fortress of Winds

entries.description:
Either it's Team Magma or Team Aqua. It depends on the version of the game. Anyway, this theme is groovy. Best used for modern looking levels. I guess it can work for castles too since this theme is originally heard when inside the antagonist's hideout.



UPDATES: Swapped a few channels around. Fixed the @21s randomly changing pitch. Tacked on $F4 $02 to make this sound way better than the previous 2 versions. Fixed the @3 that played on channel 8, which was an entire octave lower than intended.
entries.name: Pokémon Ruby/Sapphire/Emerald - Hideout

entries.description:
This is a fairly intense song from Rise of the Robots that has a industrial/factory type vibe. It has a steady drum beat with a couple different melody lines and a unison bridge about half way through. This song would work well for long and or difficult levels as the loops are long enough that it doesn't repeat the same sections quickly.



Also included is a version with shortened loops so the entire song plays in around 1:15, insert size is the same.
entries.name: Rise of the Robots - The Loader

entries.description:
This is the theme that plays at the lower depths of the Brine Cave dungeon, which contains the final floors of the dungeon before you face off against the boss (or should I say, bosses) of this dungeon. 



Basically, as the title suggests, this has a very bassy and deep feel that complements the "deep sea cave" vibe of the dungeon very nicely, and as such it would be best used in a scenario like that. Something like a sunken ship/temple deep in the depths of the sea would also fit very nicely for this.
entries.name: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time/Darkness/Sky - Lower Brine Cave

entries.description:
This is the battle theme from Rockman.exe N1 Battle for the WonderSwan Colour. This uses samples, but they're small. Except for the drums, the samples are extremely tiny and looped.

entries.description:
This is the fun and icy theme for everyone's favorite baka, Cirno, from the honestly very solid Megaman fangame Megamari, which is essentlally a crossover of sorts with the Touhou and Megaman franchise. 



This pack comes with two versions; one is a regular sampled version with some extra spacious reverb, and the other one is a version styled after Megaman 7, just in case someone wants something that feels even more Megaman-ish than the track itself; and instead of reverb, you get GAIN envelopes. Loads and loads of it. lmao



For recommendations, there's nothing much outside of what you'd normally expect from a theme like this, which means this would mostly fit in a ice level of any kind, especially one with happy undertones. However, this could also fit a grassland too. I guess.

entries.description:
The last boss's theme in the Danmakufu Touhou game "The Last Comer", Iesua Nazarenus.



Earported by yours truly (yes I can't believe I managed to make it either), fits all the kinds of those long neverending annoying final levels where you have tons of gimmicks all the time and if you die you have to redo all of it. The song itself is very long and varied, so long levels are the way to go.



Note that it's slightly different from the Idol version (available on my Youtube), since I had to downsample the biggest samples (the organ, the bell and the strings+organ sample).



Also, not compatible with Yoshi's SFX. It uses the #noYoshi sample group, except that this time it's incorporated within the .txt. No need to add stuff in Addmusic_sample_groups.txt anymore!



EDIT: Added a version that is compatible with all global songs, but with less echo.

entries.description:
My goal for 2019 is to upload more music and generally be more active... and possibly have a shot at mosts!



This is Silence, a moody piece from the original F-Zero that debuted on the SNES in 1990, 1991, and 1992 in Japan, America, and Europe respectively. It's probably one of my favorite games... Great soundtrack, and you get to slam into walls at over 3 times the interstate speed limit and uh, die... While listening to some really catchy music! Even the music that plays after you die is great



Unlike the song's name implies, there is no actual silence. It starts out rather calm, but then the second part of it drops into something less calm that would definitely fit an exciting level.



Accuracy was not in mind when I made this song!
entries.name: F-Zero - Silence

entries.description:
I really should have put some mode 7 trivia in the F-Zero port but I guess that chance has passed lol



The original Rainbow Road music from Super Mario Kart, released in mid 1992 for Japan and America and early 1993 for Europe.



It was a time when drifting physics were very different and every track was flat. Also speaking of which, if you don't know how to drift in Mario Kart then you need to figure that out asap. Please... people, drifting is important.



Did you know that there's an editor for this game too? It's called Epic Edit and I think it's actually still being maintained to this day... just checked. Last change was about a year ago. Also its open source.







This port is a little more laid-back than the real thing. It's not comatose, but it's not exactly hyper-exciting. If you want something as truly upbeat as the original, there's a nice sampled version of it somewhere on the site.



As usual, accuracy is never a priority with stuff from me.
entries.name: Super Mario Kart - Rainbow Road

entries.description:
This is a pack of music ported and SFXs ripped from Super Mario All-Stars which includes a total of 166 songs and 137 SFXs ready to be used with AMK! Musically it includes all original songs from the game, extra songs from the Game Boy Advance versions, extra songs from Mario Maker, as well a few more custom arrangements. In terms of SFX it should include all SFXs from the game with the exception of some which are hardcoded in the SPC engine ($1DFA).



All songs are ported with information regarding insert size and more on each txt. SFXs are in hex format, with exception of non-noise instrument commands. (Unfortunately it is rather hard to transform them into notes since most of them are made of pitch slides and other are joined with note length, like the volume command. Note that some SPCs are buggy, for some reason AMK dislike some noise instruments. -Vitor)



SPCs from the ost have been edited to cut out unnecessary silence and fade outs for those who download simply to listen them.



Please give credit if used.







Change Log:



7-6-19

Added some ports from Super Mario Bros. Deluxe (Album, Challenge Menu & Toy Box, and Race [sampled and unsampled]). Fixed slight tempo issues in all Ending 2 and Credit 2 variations. Redid a lot of SPC tags, mainly the advance series songs.



3-11-19

Updated all Ending 2 and Credit 2 variations. There was a channel the I forgot to enable echo on near the end.



2-17-19

Lowered the octave of the @4 in the SMB1 Airship port so the chords layer as well as SMB3's Airship theme, the unsampled version was left untouched.



1-30-19

Fixed some detuned instruments present in SMB2 and SMB3 Choose A Game port.



1-12-19

Added SMB3 Title (Unsampled).



1-10-2019 Update 2

Added 2 extra "songs", the Intro Chattering (both American and Japanese). The chattering was ported as songs rather than SFX bc there was too much technical difficulties in setting it up to make it work. Added 2 extra sfx instruments. Doomship Moving and Background Phanto's eyes glowing now work. Must add an "!" after "default/11 SMW @17.brr" and or "optimized/11 SMW @17.brr" for Doomship Moving to work and this to InstrumentData.asm under the SFXInstrumentTable (as in after the table):

db $70, $70, $00, $10, $02, $F4, $F4, $70, $02

db $70, $70, $00, $10, $11, $FA, $6A, $70, $03



1-10-2019 Update 1

Fixed mislabeled sfx. All should have the correct names and added 4F Explosion in 1DFC.



01-09-2019

Added Super Mario Bros. 2 Underground (Beta)



01-05-2019

Added $f4 $02 to the SMB2 Title theme as well as other slight text edits.



01-04-2019

Changed a few SPC timings that I forgot to take out unnecessary silence and changed a bit of incorrect info on some texts.
entries.name: Super Mario All-Stars Soundtrack: Ultimate Edition

entries.description:
This is a Dracula X styled arrangement of the first stage theme of Castlevania Bloodlines. There was technically a older version of this if you still remember that, and it was absolutely horrible, so finally, after a while I decided to remake it with my current skills. Think this definitely turned out a lot better than before lol



Use this if you want something more gothic or epic for your first level or castle; Castlevania first level music fits best for that criteria I find, haha

entries.description:
This is a arrangement of Iron Blue Intention from Castlevania Bloodlines, which is also Eric Lecarde's theme according to a lot of fans and even Konami themselves.



Use this if you need a epic final level or castle; the tubular bells at the beginning really fit well with the finality of this theme IMHO (tho it's Jorge D. Fuentes you should thank for that, not me lmao), so I think it would definitely be used well in this setting.

entries.description: This is the first Dracula stage theme from Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge. It's very fast paced and epic, which would definitely fit a chase scene and/or a "final stretch before the final boss" sorta scenario quite well.

entries.description:
This is a enhanced arrangement of Death Wind from the first F-Zero. I decided to do this because I thought the original song really deserved better instrumentation and echo to truly stand out, because the compositions themselves are actually very nice.



Use this for a area before the final boss or castle; with the wind SFX, it definitely has that vibe IMO lol

entries.description:
This is a enhanced arrangement of White Land from the first F-Zero. I decided to do this because I thought the original song really deserved better instrumentation and echo to truly stand out, because the compositions themselves are actually very nice.



Use this if you need a fast-paced chase in a winter level or something; it's not very calm, so it would probably only work on a scenario like that lol

entries.description:

While I tried to remain faithful to the original, I did have to make some adjustments, especially to the end section because there are some sound effects in the music that couldn't feseably be replicated on the Snes. For that section I improvised a sort of melody to replace the sounds I left out, so it deviates from the original a bit in that respect.

entries.description:
The very chill and jazzy Light Plane theme from a game called Pilotwings, which, thanks to Soyo Oka, has a pretty amazing soundtrack. It's honestly really surprisingly high-quality for a SNES launch title too, and it's definitely a much better example of a good SNES Nintendo soundtrack compared to most of their other works. Still, the samples could be better, which is why I gave this the resampled treatment, like I do with a lot of my other ports.



Alright, so, in this you will see two versions; one is a standard rearrangement with added flourishes of my own, and the second is a vocal version with samples I have recorded myself (I don't have any proper voice recording equipment tho, but they still get the job done :V), made specifically to mimick the vocal version in Smash 4's version.



Oh, and uh, if you need to use this, you could try using it in a sky, grassland, or early-game athletic stages, I suppose. Alright, hope y'all enjoy :D
entries.name: Pilotwings - Light Plane

entries.description:
This is Sagat's theme from Street Fighter II. It's a pretty funky song, but also very calm and fast paced (which is honestly not a combination I have ever thought I'd see in a song lmao). It also is a pretty complex song in that it's not only odd-timed, but also constantly changes time signatures throughout the whole song. AFAIK, the time signatures changes between 11/8 and 7/8, which makes this a pretty "janky" tune I suppose, but what do I know, I'm a complete illiterate at music theory lol



Oh yeah, right, I almost forgot; for this, I think a eastern level would work very well for this song, and you could also make it a athletic level if you want, your choice :V
entries.name: Street Fighter II: World Warrior - Sagat's Theme

entries.description:
A super-accurate port of Chemical Plant from Sonic 2.



This is pretty much entirely based off of Kulor's Chemical Plant SNES Cover on Youtube, So shoutouts to him, but that one was done on SNESMOD. And I thought that the song would be useful to hackers who want the song in their hack. So I decided to transcribe the .it source to AddmusicK by hand as accurately as I could, which took a few hours. 



You may notice that the pitch bends near the end of the loop are gone and are now just sustained notes. That's because I really did try to get them in, but the pitch bend command wasn't behaving like I wanted it to, so I decided to leave it alone. But if anyone else can get it to work, feel free to try.
entries.name: Sonic the Hedgehog 2 - Chemical Plant Zone

entries.description:
"Biolink estabilished; M.E.G.A System Online!"



This is the very heroic-like first level theme for the game Megaman ZX. This is one of the more electronic-like tracks from the game, and normally the SNES just isn't very good with electronic stuff as much as, say, the Sega Genesis, or pretty much any synth really, but I think I did a good job here nonetheless. Replicating the impact noises and synth shots was a pain in the ass tho, but at least it was easy enough to execute lol



Masterlink PMed me saying how he really liked the port, but he said there was some stuff that could be done to make it even better, so he fixed some stuff for me as well. So yeah, this is yet another update! Enjoy it I suppose



Oh yeah, this would go best in grassland or jungle levels, probably a sky level too, heck, even for a final level it would work well lmao

This is a bit of a enhanced version of Neo Megalopolis from Hyper Zone, a OST made by renowed composer Jun Ishikawa. It's honestly a shame there has been no ports of this OST by now, buuuuut I'm here to fix that!!!!!! And there's nothing you can do about it >:] (jk lmao)



Anyway, since I removed the SFX from the start of the song (since it was honestly not needed at all for a SMW level perspective IMO), it should be able to fit not only in space-like scenarios, but also for castle, urban, abstract and probably even airship sections too! (would probably fit best if it was also in space tho tbh)



(also, the title of the game has nothing to do with KDL3's final area, it just shares names lol; just saying before anyone starts to talk about that :V)

entries.description:
The mission-active theme from the Space Cadet pinball table of Cinematronics's Full Tilt! series.



Not as widely recognisable as the main theme, as this tune didn't survive the conversion of the game to "3D Pinball: Space Cadet" that came with Windows back in the day. But it's still a good tune, and a good complement to the main theme.



This port cribs the instrumentation from the previous Space Cadet main theme port, so ideally it should work together to put both in the same hack, for whatever purpose. (But also, this is my first port, and I wanted the head-start while I was figuring out how MML worked.)



Version 1.1 fixed a couple of typos so all the tracks are the right length now.
entries.name: Full Tilt! Space Cadet Pinball - Mission Theme

entries.description:
Yes, I know it mainly uses sawtooth waves, but that's what the original song was called.



 The song was originally made by David Murray. It was made for video on his '8-Bit Keys' channel where he reviewed a pulse wave keyboard called the Yamaha PSS-125. David Murray then had Anders Enger Jensen compose the soundtrack to his C64 game 'Planet X2', hence the simplicity here. One of those songs happened to be a remix of 'Oh No! More Square Waves!'.

entries.description:
This is a pack of music ported and SFXs ripped from Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island which includes a total of 45 songs ready to be inserted and 127 SFXs ready to be used with AMK! The pack includes all original songs from the original game and Super Mario Advance 3. In terms of SFX it should include most single channel SFXs from the game with the exception of some which are hardcoded in the SPC engine. Some examples of this include multichannel SFX as well as some that were causing problems despite the data being set right which needs further attention. Some SFX also sound slightly off tune bc YI's SFX instruments follow the same format as regular song instruments which have a subtuning multiplier which SMW does not have. Very few 2 channel SFX were kept in that didn't sound so off without its other channel.



Please give credit if used.





Change Log:



7-14-19

Fixed some typos in the readme as well as extended it to be a more descriptive. Fixed 49 Yoshi jumping which would continuously loop.
entries.name: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island Soundtrack

entries.description:
This is the theme that plays when you're fighting Richter Belmont, the game's fake final boss, in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. This is a very final-like song, but it's also a very weird and "janky" one, thanks to the 5/8 time signature this song is mostly in, which, along with the overall strong presence of dissonance, gives off a very great sense of unsettlement and tragedy to the battle itself, to differentiate from other final boss themes.



But yeah, like I said here, honestly, in my opinion, I think the best way this could fit is really only for final boss battles. You could probably find a better use for this port outside of that purpose tho, maybe I'm just being dumb. :V

entries.description:
A powerful and melancholic industrial song that plays in Shiver Star's factory stage. Makes extensive usage of ARAM, so some SMW samples have been disabled for it. I've included a more SMW compatible version for convenience.



Samples omitted: 09 SMW @7.brr, 0D SMW @14.brr, 0F SMW @21.brr, 11 SMW @17.brr, (13 SMW Thunder.brr)*.

INCOMPATIBLE WITH: Bonus End music, (Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX, Castle destruction bomb SFX)*.

*Items in parenthesis are not a concern in the more SMW compatible version.



If you need even more samples enabled, you have the option to lower the echo delay (at the cost of sound quality). Find "$F1 $03 $5C $01" in Kirby64 Factory (More SMW Compatible).txt, lower the $03, and then try re-enabling the sample you need. I suggest adjusting the echo feedback ($5C) and FIR filter ($F5 $79 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00 $00) values accordingly in case you do that.
entries.name: Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards - Factory Inspection

entries.description:
An epic and fast-paced, but at the same time, majestic final boss song. Makes extensive usage of ARAM, so some SMW samples have been disabled for it. I've included a more SMW compatible version for convenience.



Samples omitted: 09 SMW @7.brr, 0D SMW @14.brr, 0F SMW @21.brr, 11 SMW @17.brr, (13 SMW Thunder.brr)*.

INCOMPATIBLE WITH: Bonus End music, (Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX, Castle destruction bomb SFX)*.

*Items in parenthesis are not a concern in the more SMW compatible version.



If you need even more samples enabled, you have the option to lower the echo delay (at the cost of sound quality). Find "$F1 $02 $A2 $01" in Meridian Dance [Resampled] (More SMW Compatible).txt, lower the $02, and then try re-enabling the sample you need. Note, however, that $02 is already a low echo delay and decreasing it further might make the echo sound really shallow. Consider working around the custom samples instead, provided you have the knowledge or someone willing to do it.

entries.description:
This is to go even further beyond!!!



It's one of A-Ha's best known songs, Take On Me, aka the song that bops every time it's played at a party. It's been remade in a style that's supposed to be used as the music for an invincibility star.



There are two versions of the song:

- Global: This one uses @8 for the bass and @10 for the bass drum. It's optimized to work with the global songs, so you're probably gonna want to use this one if you want it to be your invincibility theme (or p-switch as well). But you can use it as your local song as well.

- Local: This one uses @14 for the bass and @21 for the bass drum. This one won't work with the global songs, but it does use a different set of instruments that some may find to be better than the global version.



This can be used as your invincibility theme, p-switch theme, bonus stage, or even as your victory jingle.
entries.name: A-ha - Take On Me (Invincibility Remix)

entries.description:
𝕾𝖙𝖎𝖑𝖑 𝖚𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖘𝖆𝖒𝖊 𝖓𝖔𝖓𝖘𝖊𝖓𝖘𝖊. 𝕹𝖔 𝖒𝖆𝖙𝖙𝖊𝖗. 𝕹𝖔𝖜 𝖎𝖘 𝖙𝖍𝖊 𝖙𝖎𝖒𝖊 𝖙𝖔 𝖕𝖚𝖙 𝖆𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊 𝖞𝖔𝖚𝖗 𝖜𝖊𝖆𝖐 𝖍𝖚𝖒𝖆𝖓 𝖘𝖎𝖉𝖊, 𝖆𝖓𝖉 𝖏𝖔𝖎𝖓 𝖒𝖊 𝖎𝖓 𝖗𝖊𝖒𝖆𝖐𝖎𝖓𝖌 𝖙𝖍𝖎𝖘 𝖜𝖔𝖗𝖑𝖉!





Bloody Tears from Worst Metroidvania ever Castlevania II: Simon's Quest. Since everyone seems to like porting the Super Castlevania IV version more than the original, I had to do my part and give you guys my rendition of the original song. Nothing way too extreme, but nothing simple either.



This song could fit intense castle levels, fast-paced levels, dark levels, and maybe even some bosses



Note: There's a !!! READ ME !!!.txt file which has the sample bank for the song. You need to copy that over to Addmusic_sample groups.txt or else the song will not work. Also you go into the song file, you can adjust the pitch to five different options that are on there: a# minor (Default), b minor (Hyper-Realistic by Lui37), a minor (Custom one but I call it "Mega Man"), g minor (I think it's custom, but I call it anyways "Touhou" because it's always about Touhou!), and f minor (Super Castlevania IV).



Also shoutouts to @springhakurei "Jeto" on twitter. Jeto makes some awesome / kawaii art on Small Richter, Touhou girls, and a lotta Simon... and I mean a lot.
entries.name: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest - Dracula's Bloodfest ~ Bloody Tears (Remix)

This song is perfect for title screens, bonus levels, credits for short and simple romhacks / fangames, and yoshi houses. If you wanna get crazy, you can put this in a cutscene as well, but it can't be a serious one though. It has to be humorous and meme-able.

entries.description:
A remix of Metal Man's stage theme from Mega Man 2, aka that one boss, Metal Man, who is known for being incredibly weak to his own weapon, the Metal Blade. He dies in a single hit.



Based off of the Wily Wars version and uses some of the Sonic 2 / Sonic 3 samples from the Yamaha YM2612 (the sound chip for the Sega Genesis / Sega Mega Drive), but also some SNES samples as well.



Factories & laboratories are obvious choices to use this in, but intense castles and retro-esque stages should work as well.
entries.name: Mega Man: The Wily Wars - Metal Blade Edge ~ Metal Man's Stage (Remix)

entries.description:
𝖂𝖍𝖆𝖙 𝖆 𝖍𝖔𝖗𝖗𝖎𝖇𝖑𝖊 𝖓𝖎𝖌𝖍𝖙 𝖙𝖔 𝖍𝖆𝖛𝖊 𝖆 𝖈𝖚𝖗𝖘𝖊!



This is an arrangement Cross Your Heart, the first stage theme from Konami's Castlevania arcade game Haunted Castle. I had this song stuck in my head for about a week and decided to let it out of my head and into a port.



This song can fit castle, factories, towers, and intense levels / scenarios.



Note:

There is a !! Read Me!!.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.

There are three customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:

- f# minor (The default pitch from the original game)

- g minor (Based on Crucifix Held Close from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin)

- e minor (A custom pitch that I thought sounded pretty cool for this song)



If you haven't already, check out Ultima's arrangement of Crucifix Held Close, a similar song from Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin. It's a well-crafted arrangement that some may prefer over this one if you liked that version better than what Haunted Castle had to offer.

Note: There's a READ ME!!.txt file with the sample group necessary for this song to work. All you need to do is copy what's inside and place it into the Addmusic_sample groups.txt file or else an error will come up when you try to export this into your romhack. This should probably fit in a lot of final scenarios specifically (like an entrance right before the final level of a hack), but not much else.

entries.description:
This is a Megaman X2 styled arrangement of the Wily Stage 1 theme from Megaman 7, also known as Wily Stage 1 ~ Entrance. While MegaNerd14 requested this song to be ported, unlike the unsampled version, this one was my own choice since I also wanted to try and do a X2 styled port of this song. :V



it sounds a bit too much like Luiz Fernando de Jesus Ribeiro's arrangement of the song tho (here's a link to it in case you're wondering: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y4DSmGiLHVo), and while I wanted to use the sax sample from X2 to differentiate this arrangement from his, it just wasn't full enough, so sadly I had to use the brass sample the same way he did; oh well, it sounds good, so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯



This should probably fit in a lot of final scenarios specifically (like an entrance right before the final level of a hack), but not much else.



EDIT: Fixed a slight issue with the marimba where it desynced slightly before the loop due to the note length being slightly off; not too noticeable, but with how fast the marimba plays in that part, it gets annoying fast :V

There's two versions of the port: one that has a sample removed and slight reduction in echo, and some SMW instruments removed, but none of the ones that are actually shared by any SFX; this is the optimized version. I still included the original version of the port tho in case anyone wants to try and insert that one.



This one probably fits well in underwater castles and ruins, preferably places which are tense and dramatic enough to fit the song. Outside of that, I don't have many ideas. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

entries.description:
This is Splash Wave from OutRun, A.K.A that one game everyone knows about by name but knows jack shit about it otherwise... well, some people may know about the soundtrack at least, it's considered a classic by many after all LOL



For this one, I, of course, decided to put my own spin on this theme by adding a lot of my own embellishments based around my own musical style (A.K.A tons of drum syncopation and focus on drums in general), so it's not *too* accurate to the original, but I hope people still enjoy this :D



Anyway, this is a absolute LONG boi, so if you want to use this in a level it's got to match up with the length of the song; outside of that, this could be used for beach, final, or just long ass levels in general, but of course, it could also be used as a credits/staff roll theme as well because of the length, so it's pretty multipurpose, which could make the long size a bit more worth it :P



EDIT: Along with the alternate loop version, there's now a no legato version in case the melody gets cut after the song gets paused; those are separate mainly so that people can use those versions in case your hack has the entire song silenced wherever you pause the game (A.K.A what SMW normally does by default), and the normal versions are for hacks that doesn't silence the entire song when you pause the game.

entries.description:
The acid house inspired level theme at the last portion of Round 3 in Streets of Rage 2. A good song for any dark and spooky area, or any level where you wanna make a strange tonal shift in the environment or something.



All samples are technically from SMW - two of them are chorded @0s (to consolidate channel space), one is a pitch bent @0 kick made into a sample to reduce pitch bend spam (and by extension, potential lag from AMK) and one is a pitch bent @0 kick layered with @29. Due to how the channels are set up, an ill-timed sound effect around 1:01 in may result in the instrument not changing as it should, but the issue corrects itself within a matter of seconds.

entries.description:

entries.description:
The really repetitive song from fifth stage of the 8-bit Sonic 2, whose level aesthetic bears several similarities to Scrap Brain Zone from the first Sonic game. As such, it works well with mechanical/factory areas or something.



The port was originally completed on November 5th, 2015 as part of SMWCentral Idol 7 Round 2, where it took first place. The challenge, for those curious, was to port or compose a song that didn't use any SMW samples, as well as requisite use of at least three NES samples. The only audible differences between this version and the Idol submission are mixing, and a quicker volume fade for the intro square waves. 



The arrangement, a MIDI by King Meteor, differs from the original as it adds chords and a few extra flourishes at the end.

Special thanks to Nameless for helping me experiment with the lead instrument.

entries.description:
The spooky but fun music from probably the most grandiose New Super Mario Bros. Wii hack. It's one of those songs that's not dramatic for the sake of dramatic, but rather sort of suspenseful, and weirdly, groovy.



The lead is technically an octave higher than it should be, but it sounds fuller I find, and because unsampled SMW harps would sound way too muddy at a lower octave. Features unsampled cricket noises too, yeehaw.



Also used in Luigi Goes Trick-or-Treating from HLDC 2019.



Note: AMK does not like the cricket noises nor the vibrato, and the song may lag out a bit when the timer drops below 100. There are three versions of the port; one "full" one, one with less crickets, and one with less vibrato. The less vibrato version is probably the best to circumvent tempo hike slowdown while still maintaining a decently full sound.
entries.name: Newer Super Mario Bros. Wii - Pumpkin

entries.description:
A dreamy song that's very un-WarioWare like, all things considered, but fits right in with the microgame it plays in. It has that sparkly, aesthetic-y touch that's probably good for any form of calm night level. I also feel like this is one of those ports that brings out the best in some of the more underrated SMW instruments, such as @3 and @9.



On a more technical side, this port required a lot of cramming things together into one channel, despite its apparent simplicity.
entries.name: WarioWare: Touched! - Rainbow Juice

Here's another one of many obscure SNES ports that people make all the time in this site which most people barely even give a fuck when it comes to the game and even the soundtrack itself outside of the fact this one port "sounds cool"...

entries.description:
And here's something I don't think anyone here would expect: a remix (no, it's not an arrangement this time, I mean an actual remix) of the final boss theme from Megaman ZX, Pallida Mors. This one was made for a certain competition for the Chiptune Cafe Discord server, and since it's been a while that the competition ended, I think it's a good enough opportunity to release this now haha



Anyway, this one is very different to the original in many different ways, but the biggest change specifically is the extra section I've added at 2:47. Since this was made mainly thinking about the competition itself and not specifically for SMW, it doesn't loop like the original does. Despite that tho, I have made a looped version for it, and honestly, the song is long enough by it's own that it fits it's purpose well enough to work even without the loop.



There's also optimized versions for each version as well; these don't have the echo and removes a few SFX samples, like Yoshi bongos and the thunder SFX, but I feel like it could be done better than this, I just couldn't be bothered really lmao



But anyway... this one I feel like it could only really work in a final boss setting, but the looped version is there if you want to use it for a level pretty much. Not much else to say here, just have fun :P
entries.name: Mega Man ZX - Pallida Mors

entries.description:
A very tropical-sounding song from Treasure Hunter G! A quick and simple song because I haven't ported anything in a while!



I included two versions of the port: the one I recommend using, and one with halved tempo. The latter doesn't have any slowdown, but it's slightly faster because of the engine's inaccurate tempo values (-1 and it's too slow; +1 and it's too fast). The slowdown in the original version is very minimal, but it might bother some people. It's kind of a "pick your poison" situation though...

entries.description:
A more thrilling remix of the Underground/Temple/Ruins theme from Super Mario Land, based off of the midi by Andy Smith.



Because of how ridiculous the chords and drums are in the midi, I opted out for a series of 6 samples of chords and a drum track sample instead of trying to mash around 13+ channels worth of instruments. I ended up making almost all the samples, but feel free to use 'em in your own works. (All the samples except for the Orchestral Crash Cymbal originate from the Timbres of Heaven soundfont)



Incompatible with Bonus end, Blarggs, Thunder, and Yoshi.



Mod edit: Tempo will not increase when the timer is running low.

This game was basically based of Malibu Comics of the same protagonist/universe name. An alpha build was shown in a C3, and then it got cancelled very early.

This song is undoubtely very raw, compared to other Follin works, but I wanted to port it anyway.

I recommend using it in a very short level or anything very short like a Hub, overworld or something else.



An optimized version is included where it just removes the two channels which amplifies both the drums and the guitar sounds.

entries.description:
An extra track that was composed by Tsuyoshi Sekito for the Playstation port of said game. It's listened on the music box of the extras menus.

Due to the original song having much more than 8 channels, I decided to separate it into two versions, one for the Pianos and other for the Choir ones. If you want to use the Choirs, change the Choir_Version define to 1.

Also, because this song is very heavy in sample usage, I had to downsample the Choir, Piano and the String Ensemble samples to make it compatible with most of vanilla SFX.

Anyway, an unoptimized version is also included.



Requested by BootaNoBijuu/Neo Bonobi.

This song works best in castles, factories, towers, final areas, & other levels with intense vibes.

There is a ADD ME TO ADDMUSICK.txt file that has the sample bank that you need to move to Addmusic_sample_groups.txt. Thunder and Yoshi sound effects are disabled.

There are two customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song file:

- e minor (the default pitch specifically for this remix)

- d minor (The original pitch from the games)

A song that goes back and forth between a hesitant calmness and an energetic main melody. Probably best suited for athletic or sky levels, though the song does have a certain emotion to it that's not just blindly happy. With the way the tempo increases at times, it especially suits very fast-paced levels.

entries.description:
A jazzy song beat like movies, drama, news, tv show, and other media activities. This song has a specific of Blues-Style, High Tempo (but halved tempo in this port because of laggy). This song has two verses [Synth Trumpet and Piano].

This song could be fit the carnival, casino, park, restaurant, city, palace, town, hotel, disco, and house levels during the dusk. also fit on cutscenes, title screen, or credits



Remember that, There have two different versions:

Version 1: One Loop [Short Version] (0x0700 = 1792 bytes, 0:49 Seconds)

Version 2: Two Loops [Normal Version] (0x09DB = 2523 bytes, 1:32 Seconds)

Loop Start = Second 0:05



Update 2020-05-25: Channel 7 has swapped into Channel 6 because noise overclock may glitch for dino-torches when blowing fire (requested by yupyup____)

entries.description:
A quiet, haunting song that plays in a final dungeon. Useful for finals, temples and night levels.



Trivia:

- My favourite dungeon in the game.

- I spent 30% of production time trying to fix one mistake in the midi file.

- Big thanks to user @Brozilla for teaching me $FA$02$XX some months ago because I abused it to save memory space. Also it made the code organizing a cakewalk! :))

- Again big thanks to user @musicalman for his sample pack.

- After @Tamaki's suggestion, I made the instrumentation closer to the original's. I still do not own the original samples (@Samantha), so I'll leave it as "remix" and try to get started in sample ripping.

- Update 27/05: fixed the notes at the end and the bell octave at the beginning.

entries.description:
I originally made this song for a 100% free (with no in-game-real-money payments) sidescroller MMORPG game called Aeon Rivals back in 2017 when it was in development.



It was originally for the Lost Desert level, as the author was requesting for .XM music to be put into the game. 



I gave the author this song and while he liked it, he couldn't put it in the game because I was 14 at the time, so I was too young to be able to receive payment without complications.



Of course, I'm still too young now, and it seems the game is already done, so I'll just upload the song here. Well, converted to AddMusicK MML.



This might not sound like most other desert themes. I tried to go not for the classic Saharan feel, but for a more southern US atmosphere that is also mysterious.



And yes, I lifted the drum samples from Evanescence's Bring Me To Life stems.
entries.name: Lost Desert

entries.description:
A remix of Ice Cap Zone Act 1 (Genesis version) from Sonic 3 & Knuckles. This time, it's stylized after the original song it's based off of: Hard Times by The Jetzons. This one took me a while to make, & it was worth it! :D



I absolutely love this song, & despite there already being many different remixes of this song on here, I wanted to add one more into that mix with a new twist. It's my favorite song from the "Sonic 3" half of the game (making it my 3rd favorite in the entire soundtrack) and one of my favorite ice stage themes in any video game, though I guess the fact that this song is based on an old vocal makes sense why this bangs so hard!!!



This song can fit in intense winter themed stages (ice, snow, etc.). Also great for RADICAL snowboarding stages.



Important:

♠ There is a "READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into Addmusic_sample_groups.txt.

♠ Thunder SFX is disabled.

entries.description:
The uncertainly strong stage 1 theme from Shuusou Gyoku, which has a heavy sense of an adventure beginning. Would probably best fit early-game levels with somewhat of a more serious tone. The key of the song is also based on the ZUN's later arrangement, although slightly flat because I felt it gave it a certain charm. The mixing is mostly based on SC-88 recordings of the song, though there's some sprinkles of the GM mixing as well.



On the technical side, this was an intersting song to port because, 8 channels barely being enough aside, there are lots of sections where there's tons of channels of @1 playing together, which thankfully don't overlap (somehow).



I took some slight liberties with the panning, especially with the square waves, since the original uses a lot of same-note/different-instrument channels panned away from each other (which I didn't have space for here), and had a lot of the unique channels exclusively panned to the left, which would end up a bit obnoxious.

entries.description:
A beautiful and heavenly sounding song that plays in Sky Tower, the final dungeon of the main story. Makes extensive usage of ARAM, so some SMW samples have been disabled for it. Comes in four versions of txt:



- SMW Compatible: has the best quality of the bunch, but isn't compatible with Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX and Castle destruction bomb SFX. Additionally, it uses noise instruments that affect noise-based SFX, like Fire Spit SFX, Podoboo SFX and Koopaling land in lava SFX.



- Noise SFX Compatible: uses a noise sample instead of the regular SPC700-generated noise, meaning it won't affect noise-based SFX. The other alternative to circumvent the issue would be to send all the noise instruments to channel 8, but then the song would suffer noticeable cuts every time the jump SFX played.



- Blargg & Thunder Compatible: at the cost of some echo delay, it is compatible with Blargg roar SFX, Thunder SFX, Valley of Bowser appears SFX and Castle destruction bomb SFX.



- Most Compatible: a combination of the previous two versions.



All versions are incompatible with the Bonus End music.

Samples omitted: 09 SMW @7.brr, 0D SMW @14.brr, 0F SMW @21.brr, 11 SMW @17.brr, (13 SMW Thunder.brr)*.

*Only for the SMW Compatible and Noise SFX Compatible versions.



I've also included the SPC of the original port for listening purposes. Enjoy!

A remix of the famous Dr. Wily's Castle 1 from Mega Man 2 (mostly based off the Wily Wars version) ft. Sanae Kochiya's theme, Faith is for the Transient, from Touhou 10: Mountain of Faith. I love Wily's Castle 1 to death. It's one of my favorite VGMs of all-time, and I've been wanting to do a remix of this song for ages. I had such a fun time working on this, and I decided to incorporate Sanae's theme in there because her theme song always reminded me of this song.



This song is perfect for castle stages, tower stages, castle grounds stages, airship stages, intense stages, space, and final areas.



Note:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."
