entries.description:
Or I guess I should call it Blue Hills of an Ancient Century ~ Here We Go!



My entry to 120hoSPC #7, a heavy remix of the SMW overworld theme that we've all grown tired of that transforms it into a Touhou song. Featuring hallmarks of Touhou music such as phrases turning from minor to major in their resolution, sections that repeat but a semitone higher, sections that repeat but chorded, a "midboss appearance" part that changes the tone a bit, and a big elaborate piano solo at the end.



This song started out with the theme of autumn in mind, so I suppose it could fit in those kinds of levels pretty well. Otherwise, it could fit in any long and somewhat tense level.



If you're looking for over-the-top Touhou music for your World 1-1 Grassy Grass Grasslands, then look no further!

Did a remix of New Messiah from Castlevania II: Belmont's Revenge. Promised myself that I'd do more Castlevania remixes (the jingles I did don't count) since the last song I did was Don't Wait Until the Night, and that was right before my music actually started to get better. I haven't played the Gameboy Castlevania games that much, but I have listened to New Messiah quite a bit, and it's actually a pretty good track, so I thought I'd remix that for this time. Only took me a couple hours to do surprisingly.



This song is perfect for castle, factory, castle grounds, and tower stages.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- @7, Thunder, and Yoshi SFX are disabled.



Update:

9/9/2020 - Fixed tempo to work with AMK 1.0.7

Yes, I did a remix of Chase from Jojo's Bizarre Adventure (Part 4): Diamond is Unbreakable. You're not seeing things. It's my favorite of the Jojo OP themes and is by far one of the most underrated ones in the series. The hard rock combined with the deep emotion set piece really sets the mood for the entire song. Note, this isn't the actual full song and is just based on the OP version, since doing the full song would take up so much ARAM.



This baby can fit title screens, credits, [final] boss fights, intense stages, final areas, and castle / towers stages.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- "Bonus End" is disabled.



There's also an option to enable or disable the loop in the song file with an ending like in the OP:

1. Loops the song (turned on by default).

2. No Loop
entries.name: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Diamond is Unbreakable - Chase ~ Opening 2 (Remix)

entries.description:
A remix of Dr. Wily's Castle from Mega Man 5. I love this song. It's my 2nd favorite castle theme in the entire Mega Man franchise, and it's amazing. The dark tone of the song really sets the mood for these last four stages of the game, while also keeping the player from stopping with its robust melodies that accompany the tone. Yeah, I'm part of the "Wily's Castle > Dark Man's Fortress" gang. Even if Mega Man 5 is already an amazing game, this song is one of the reasons for me to replay the game.



This song is perfect for factories, castles, towers, and final areas.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- "Bonus End," Yoshi SFX, & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also 3 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. G / C Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. F# / B Minor (Custom Pitch 1)

3. G# / C# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)



Update:

10/23/2020 - Adjusted the tempo for AMK 1.0.7 and added the option to customizable pitch with three options.

entries.description:
I don't think I have ever been as happy with my any of my remixes until except for my most recent MM5 Wily's Castle Remix. I had so much fun with that one (if what I said in that port's description didn't convince that already), and I just really wanted to kinda do it again, so I remade it into an unsampled remix (the second time I have both an unsampled and sampled port of the same song). Like I said before, this is by far one of the best Mega Man themes in the entire franchise.



This song is perfect for dark, city, castle, castle ground, tower, space, and factory stages.

entries.description:
A happy motivational battlefield theme where you can imagine infantry going on a rampage, in fact that's exactly how it was used in the original game, but also with dragons, so it is more epic. You can also see it fit for overworlds and titles.



I'm happy to present you this song because that's literally the only one that I kept as a memory from when I played the game in late 2011, that's a damn good earworm.



This was my most appreciated track in Super Famicompo 2, with a ranking of 21/46 in the cover category. After voters' comments, I have upgraded it a bit, I believe.
entries.name: Bahamut Lagoon - Orerusu Salvation Army

entries.description:
So it is supposed illustrate a temple in space that's also evil and the fnal level of the game.



This track could find some use in a specific set of Mario levels and overworlds that occur in space or abstract places, I can imagine well in Kaizo too.



It ranked 31/46 at Super Famicompo 2 and I used voters' comments to upgrade a bit. Though, I could not find more fitting samples for my sampling light, and I happen to like this clarinet very much.

Now, that's just the audio without the actual scene, lmao.

There's an endless version included inside both text files, in case you want to use it forever. If you want to use the endless version, change the Endless_Elevator define to 1.

Did a remix of Jet Stringray's Stage from Mega Man X4. Worst Maverick stage in the game, but goddamn, this song bangs so freaking hard, I can't help but forgive it because of it... until I have to get that damn subtank!!!



This baby is great for beach stages, athletic / sky stages, intense stages, boss fights, and auto-running stages.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

entries.description:
Did a remix of Kraid's Lair from Metroid. Just started getting into the Metroid series as of recently, but I've been a fan of this song ever since I first heard it in Super Smash Bros Melee in the early 2000s (how I was introduced to the series).



This baby is great for caverns, dark castles / towers, and dark cutscenes.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.
entries.name: Metroid - Heart of a Titan ~ Kraid's Lair (Remix)

entries.description:
Did a remix of At Doom's Gate ~ E1M1 from DOOM (MS-DOS version). Do I need to tell you how great this song is? It's one of gaming's most popular songs. You definitely have heard this before in some form.



This baby is great for [final] boss fights, tense stages, lava caverns, factories, castles / towers, final areas, chase sequences, and anything else badass 80s metal can fit in.



Important:

There are also 2 customizable loop options for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. Remix (loops at 00:18)

2. Original (loops from the very beginning of the song)
entries.name: Ultimate DOOM - At Doom's Gate ~ E1M1 (Remix)

entries.description:
Did another unnecessarily intense and silly remix of a world map theme from Super Mario Bros. 3. This time, it's Ocean Side (World 3). Idk why I decided to do this, especially after doing my other silly Giant Land (World 4) remix a couple months back, but it's here. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯



This baby is great for seaside / beach world maps, seaside / beach stages, and disco stages.



Important:

There are also 2 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. C Major (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. B Major (A Link to the Past Pitch

3. A# Major (Ocarina of Time Pitch)

Did a remix of Wily's Capsule from Mega Man 4, and it's another one of my Touhou X Mega Man mashup things. Still one of my favorite final boss themes (as well as Flight of the Bamboo) in any video game, despite its short length. Really gives off a dark and intense vibe throughout the entire fight, despite it being one of the easiest Mega Man final bosses in the entire series.



This baby is great for boss fights, final bosses, chase sequences, and intense stages.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- Thunder SFX is disabled.



There are also 2 customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. F Major (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. F# Major (Custom Pitch)

entries.description:
The song that inspired Chrono Trigger's Corridors of time, ported in the style of Corridors of time. Very mystic, atmospheric, contemplative. I invite you to listen to the original versions by Joe Hisaishi. Useful for ruins, deserts and cave overworlds.



Trivia:



After humming corridors of time all the time, I did have my epiphany, found the similarity between the two, and decided to go for it.

This took a good bunch of hours trying to re-create melody from ear.

In the mix I added some elements from Corridors of Time, and also some elements from "Ohmu", the track from the image album. Below are the sources:

- Original soundtrack's "A princess who loves insects", starts at 1:00

- Image album's track "Ohmu", used as inspiration for the pitch bends.

- Re-mastered version
entries.name: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind - A Princess Who Loves Insects (Chrono Trigger Mix)

entries.description:
The theme composed specifically for the 10th place entry of VLDC12. While the original level is a fiery cave factory, you can use this in a lot of various scenarios (a tyranical jungle, a space mine, a dysfunctional castle, etc). Uses percussion samples from the end credits theme (not naming because it has a rude title) of the movie adaptation of "Land of the Lost".

Note: By setting the define for staccato define to 1, you will decrease the song size to "0x06CD". However the song will inevitably sound worse (but it'll be accurate to how it sounded in the contest entry of the same name). The surround define is more or less a preference.

A quite infamous song due to Japanese hacks, now available in AMK format! This could be used in fast-paced space and/or industrial levels, especially if they're in the long side, as the song goes on for quite some time.



Due to how busy all channels are in certain parts of the song, I had to take measures to reduce slowdown, such as disabling and enabling vibrato multiple times, as well as removing the 

Remote Commands entirely.

entries.description:
Did a remix of the first stage theme from Touhou 15: Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom, Unforgettable, the Nostalgic Greenery. One of the best soundtracks in the mainline series if you ask me, & this song is perfect for the game and stage it's being used in. Touhou 15 is known for being one of the, if not the, most difficult game in the entire series, and this song doesn't slouch on that with its high energy & tense beats, making sure you know that this game ain't gonna be like the other Touhou games.



But that's enough of my rambling 😄. Hope you enjoy this remix!!



This baby is great for grassland, athletic / sky, night, tense, and factory stages.



Important:

There is a "!READ ME.txt" file that has the sample bank. You'll need to move what's in that file into "Addmusic_sample_groups.txt."

- "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.

entries.description: The mellow tutorial theme from Knuckles' Chaotix. Good for rest areas and tutorials, and anywhere else where the player can just relax. entries.description: The lovely stage 2 theme from Mrs. Estacion, an off-brand clone of Touhou. As its name implies, this song suits any form of adventuring level, maybe with a bit of emotion in it. I always picture a sunny summer sky alongisde a bus ride through the wind when listening to this song. I'm particularly proud of the @5 Reed Romance around 0:50. Also, that piano was a pain to transcribe due to how muffled it gets at parts in the original, but I guess that's Touhou music for ya. :P

entries.description:
The somewhat mysterious, beep-y boop-y music that plays in some areas in Lyle in Cube Sector. Good for mysterious, beep-y boop-y areas like caverns or factories.



I could not make up my mind on what to do for the instrumentation, so there's two defines you can change at the top of the file, resulting in a whopping 8 different instrument combinations. Some are more experimental than others, and some bass/lead combinations sound better than others, but that's the perk of customizability!

entries.description:
The happy and calm, sparkly music that plays in Botanic Base in Knuckles' Chaotix. Good for any kind of peaceful or chill night level, though I suppose you could put it in some difficult kaizo level to calm the player down too, heh.



I ported this for me and E-man38's VLDC12 level, Greehouse Effect, but I just love this song so much that I probably would've done it even without that level.
entries.name: Knuckles' Chaotix - Midnight Greenhouse

entries.description:
An original song I made for Superfamicompo 2. This song originally started out as a discount version of Stardust Speedway (Present) from Sonic CD (JP/EU), but it sort of drifted off into its own chaotic thing. I admittedly felt very uninspired throughout the month that I was working on this, which you can probably tell by the various shifts in mood throughout the song, but I'm generally still satisfied with how the song turned out, and I think each section has its charm. I love sawtooth waves, so it was fun to make a song with one as the lead.



Overall, this song probably fits night levels, perhaps ones centered around speed, and maybe highways? That's the visual I had when composing.
entries.name: Mustard Motordrive

entries.description:
Probably best known as the invincibility theme from Sonic The Next Level, which is a hack of Sonic 1 with a lot of polish, including CD-quality music. This port is just a 30-second section of the song, just like the Sonic The Next Level version.



This song is probably best suited for happy and hopeful areas, like bonus rooms or overworlds, or maybe a sky.



You can probably use this as an invincibility theme as well, but you'll most likely have to lower the echo delay to avoid a pause, as well as add @21 as a global sample. It also lasts much longer than the vanilla star duration.

(Edit: added an additional version that uses a @0 kick.)

The "Extra stage" theme from the game-without-a-game, Touhou-style music album, Heavenly Gathering of Clouds.



It's a suspenseful but energetic song, and one that keeps getting more excited as it goes along. It's probably good for fast, night stages. I just imagine a dark purple, for some reason.

entries.description:
The "title screen" theme from Deified Submarine Palace, a fake Touhou game that was made based on rumours of Touhou 13 being water-themed. Calm and with plenty of seashore noises, this is probably best-suited for title screens, possibly beach-y ones. Like most Touhou title screen themes, it features the Theme of Eastern Story motif.



Like the responsible music mod that I am, this has two simultaneous channels of noise playing at parts where the cymbal and seashore overlap. It's designed around it so that it doesn't sound bad, but it's still important to note. Also, the seashore sound is on #7, so SFX will cut it out very easily.



(I can't find any translations of this game's song names anywhere, so I translated it myself. Let me know if there's improvements to be made.)



7 May 2022 edit: actually includes the samples now

One of Follin's best works on the SNES, this long track doesn't really fit into any level theme, but maybe it could work in an urban/athletic setting.

I tried my best to replicate everything, and considering the limitations of the N-SPC engine I think it turned out fairly accurate.



Note: not compatible with thunder sfx/Blarggs or with the "Bonus end" global song.



Update:

- Added sample group.

- Compiled with AMK 1.0.8, so the SPC doesn't have slowdown.

- Removed staccato in a bunch of places. Now the bass is THICC like in the original, but it also has a bit of noticeable clicking.

- Small edits/fixes.

entries.description:
A lively song that represents a friendly fortress located in the middle of the desert. SMW samples make it sound a it more goofy than it should, making it even more light-hearted. Technically my problem was only having @3 by my side to represent two completely different xylophone instruments from the original. More precisely I had tried with some wood block but it didn't do the job well, therefore I settled for another ADSR variation of @3. Most suitable for overworlds. Maybe something loosely related to water like lakes or water palaces.

entries.description:
This sounds more like a sky song than a casino song. For me it has a strong Tails characterization.

I could not have done that without my heavy use of musicalman's samples, so big thanks on that.



Requested by user OrangeBronzeDaisy.

entries.description:
A friendly tune to be played in desert or jungle settings, sounds like adventure.



I cannot believe how tedious and grindy it was to try myself on this and honest I was feeling like I reached my limits. It features a lot of instrument changes among each channel, and deciphering the clues I got on the original spc about pan or vibrato, was a chore too. Re-working it with Trials of Mana samples was definitely an interesting task, and I found out Trials of Mana neither has proper claps, nor a bassoon. So the aesthetic I went for here is more similar to desert tracks like Harvest November, that rely very much on flute.



It is released for the Winter C3. (re-work)



@7 (Bonus End Fanfare) has been omitted.

♠ There are two versions of the song that I've included in the zip (as separate text files):

 1. Original (It has no loop, so you'll have to adjust the invincibility / p-switch timer if you want to use this.)

entries.description:
The long repetitious bonus final level theme from Krack The Hack with a very long name to boot, originally made for Mario Must Die 3 until Sokobansolver decided to use a different theme instead. Made to be exciting training music made to fit multiple environments. There are a few differences between this version and the version in Krack The Hack itself as a result of optimizing the port for a public release.



A "no staccato" define option is present for those who wants to save space. With staccato set to 1, it'll decrease the size to 0x03A8 but will sound slightly worse (but accurate to how it was heard in Krack The Hack).



Taking a page off of Hooded Edge, there are two versions: an E Minor version (Krack pitch), and a D minor version (Daizo pitch). Pick either or to match your level as you wish!



This song isn't compatible with every SMW sample, but you're free to enable/disable what you need using the provided defines. By default I enabled LevelClear, Star, Death, and GameOver; which leaves out Thunder, Blargg, P-switch, Star, Bonus End, and Yoshi.

entries.description:
A lengthy and complex prog-rock-influenced track from Secret of Mana, composed by Hiroki Kikuta. This song uses a method of composition called "beat displacement", in which the percussion is designed so that the snares/hi-hat hits have inconsistent patterns and never land on the same beat. This made the first two channels of this song an absolute nightmare to transcribe. If I've made any errors on that front, I apologize and will fix them if they're pointed out to me. Otherwise, this is a more-or-less identical recreation of the original song.



This could work in a relaxed level, perhaps fitting especially well in a jungle/forest or beach stage. I could also see it being at home in an overworld or town setting.



Due to issues with ARAM limitations, the original SMW samples @7 and Thunder are overwritten. If you need to use those samples with this song, however, then enough room can be made simply by removing/reducing the echo effect.



Requested by Brutapode89.

entries.description:
The deeply menacing theme representing the Mako Factory from Final Fantasy VII, or as I like to call it "Magitek Research Facility's Younger Brother". Not accurate to the original due to not having the proper samples, so I used some of my own ones. Since I really like the Remake version, I included a small nod to it that plays every second loop if you enable it using the define "LOOP2" (see txt for details). If it's disabled, the size will decrease to 0x042D and the real length will be 1:35.



Includes the option to enable/disable staccato with the staccato define. With it enabled, the size will decrease to 0x05C6 (which really isn't much). If this is enabled along with LOOP2 disabled, it will become 0x0467.



This submission accounts for the max size and length using the various defines.



Song not compatible with P-switch, Bonus End, Thunder, Yoshi, or Blarggs.



Edit: Wrong notes been corrected (to the best of my abilities), tho I kept in the "wrong intro notes" as an option in the "ACCURATE" define because I unironically liked it better. Nameless is the one to thank for pointing where I made mistakes. With ACCURATE disabled (setting it to 1), it'll add 3 extra bytes.

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Wily's Castle from Mega Man 6. Got the idea to do this after humming this with some buddies in a voice call one night, and I'm glad I did. It's my favorite track in the game and another criminally underrated Wily theme.



Just like Wily's Castle in Mega Man 5, this also another one of the more emotional castle stage themes in the series, but unlike that theme, which was more upbeat and dark, this one is more slow and melancholic, which I think it fits well with the stages it's used in, given this is supposedly "the greatest battle of all-time" and Wily's final attempt at World Domination at the time (before MM7 became a thing).

Upbeat space music with a lot of retro noises.



While "surfing" on vgmusic's NES section I fell in love with this midi sequenced by user Steven C. King. I didn't know the original song at all! The midi didn't show all the accuracy it should because it uses chords in place of Follin's famous arpeggios. Therefore, later I may or may not beat the Famitracker .nsf import of the song. For the time being I improved a bit from the midi content by featuring more noise and fuller pitch bends.

Did an arrangement of the second stage in Wily's 10th fortress, Against the Pressure. To call myself a big Mega Man fan and not having done a single remix of one of the five fortress bangers from this game is essentially a cardinal sin (in my book). All these songs are amazing for many reasons (EVERY. SINGLE. ONE. IS. FANTASTIC.).



Against the Pressure perfectly sets the tone for the stage it's used in. You've entered inside the fortress now, things start to heat up, and an intense song starts playing in the background.

Did an arrangement of the third stage in Wily's 10th fortress, No Turning Back. Doing that Against the Pressure remix really set me in the mood to do another MM10 remix.



I love this theme, it's my 2nd favorite song in the entire game (behind Nitro Rider) and my favorite of the six fortress themes. It has a space-y yet dark vibe going for it, as if this song was some sort of sequel to Wily's Castle from Mega Man 5.

Did an arrangement of the first stage in Wily's 10th fortress, Abandoned Memory. Third time I've done one of the fortress themes from this game (in a row), and it was worth it!!! As I mentioned before, all the six fortress themes in this game are amazing, and this one is no exception.



Abandoned Memory really has this dark and intense tone, especially after the song that played before this, that really fits the kind of fortress Wily has put up this time and really shows you what kind of songs you're gonna be hearing throughout this entire thing. I love it, by far my 3rd favorite theme in the entire game (2nd fav. fortress theme behind No Turning Back).

Did an arrangement of another Touhou 10 theme (It's Mega Man 10 all over again. lmao) the fourth stage, Fall of Fall ~ Autumnal Waterfall. Did this for a friend of mine since he was a big fan of this song, and so am I. It's a really good stage theme and also a popular song to use in SMW romhacks (not complaining :)).



It's intense, upbeat, energic, and jolly. What more can you ask for song that plays while you're scaling a Waterfall like it's Donkey Kong Country 3. It's fantastic and there's a reason why it's probably the most popular stage theme from this game.

𝐀𝐫𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐰𝐚𝐭𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠'𝐞?



Did an arrangement of the last stage theme in Touhou 15: Legacy of the Lunatic Kingdom, The Sea Where One's Home Planet Reflects. Originally planned on doing Junko's boss theme, but given the length of the song and the fact I love making sampled arrangements, I thought I'd maybe try that later and instead do her stage theme for this round.



A beautifully crafted song that clearly takes some inspiration from David Wise (Jungle Hijinks, Klomp Romps, Stilt Village GBA). It not only contrasts the chaos of Clownpiece's stage, but also resembles the purity within Junko and the tragedy in her backstory. I praise Touhou 15's OST for having hype and upbeat songs that combine the techno and eastern styles, and this is another song that perfectly showcases that.

𝗡𝗼 𝗰𝗼𝗽𝘆𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗹𝗮𝘄 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝗺𝗲!



Did an arrangement of Aquarium Park Act 1 from Sonic Colors. With all the hype surrounding Sonic Colors Ultimate / the series 30th anniversary and the remix to this theme being showcased recently, I had to arrange this song, and Jesus! This might have been my most difficult one yet, which was amazing!!



This song is beautiful. It has a calm yet sad tone with some super freaking catchy melodies to accompany it. It perfectly fits the water-type zone and is a song that'll stay in your head even after you turn off that Wii console. It also brings brings back memories of me buying this game (along with Kirby's Epic Yarn) as a kid and spending hours on both games. I still love this game a ton and was my first introduction to the boost formula games.

The somewhere-between-serious-and-cheerful second photo theme of the 9.5th Touhou game, Shoot the Bullet.

The repetitive and loosely tense third photo theme from the 9.5 Touhou game, Shoot the Bullet.



I picture this song just as the title describes it, sitting somewhere, doing the same thing over and over again while it's dark outside, feeling completely blank inside. But maybe that's just from me replaying the parts of the game where this plays over and over again.

Probably my favourite Touhou extra boss theme.

An original song composed for NopeContest and I's KLDC2021 level, Hazy Halls.



The level in question's a cloudy, purple ghost house, and that's pretty much the vibe I went for when composing, but alongside a sense of determination too.



Most of the song is upbeat, with a small calm bit in the middle, with everything separated by some messy parts. It's also sparkly.



Probably best suited for longer levels, specifically un-serious ones, I guess?

𝗔𝘁𝘁𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗺𝗲 𝗶𝗳 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗱𝗮𝗿𝗲, 𝗜 𝘄𝗶𝗹𝗹 𝗰𝗿𝘂𝘀𝗵 𝘆𝗼𝘂!



Did a special arrangement of Ken Masters' Theme from Street Fighter II': World Warrior for my 1K subscriber milestone. I'm a massive Ken fan (maining him in every game that he's in), so I thought I'd do his theme for this special. I've been wanting to arrange this song ever since I first got into the SMW porting scene and tried so many times, but each attempt was a fail... until now. It's one of my favorite VGMs of all-time, and I'm just incredibly happy to have finally done it.



The intense energy this song is packing is perfect for Ken's fire-y spirit. I really wanted to try basing this off the CPS1 original since not only does the song fit perfectly on the F minor, but the use of mostly just synths helps give this version an identity of its own and would work best with my style, especially when compared to the SNES "Turbo" version, which heavily utilized a riff guitar and other organic instruments. (though it is still my favorite version of Ken's theme to this date). I especially prefer this over his Super Street Fighter II versions, since they mostly just sounded like "traditional CAPCOM" fair instead of a theme that fits Ken's character (plus, it just sounds weaker on the D minor / C# minor too, if you ask me).



Important:

2. F# Minor (Special Championship Edition Pitch)

An upbeat and more tense remix of Rockfish's first dev log song.

Original description by PixelOriginal:

 ボスBGM

BGMはピストンコラージュから出力した制限付き形式を使う。

今のところ、三角波 ＋ 矩形波 ＋ ノコギリ波 ＋ バスドラム ＋ ハイハット(クローズ)の計５音。

60フレームで割り切れるビート・テンポを使用。

小さいスピーカーでは低音が聴き取りにくい。

でもそれにあわせてボリューム調整をすると、今度はイヤホンがつらい。

矩形波やノコギリ波は低音でも目立つけど耳が痛い..

Rough translation:

 Boss BGM

BGM uses the restricted format output from PxTone.

So far, there are a total of 5 sounds: triangle wave + square wave + sawtooth wave + bass drum + hi-hat (closed).

Uses a beat tempo that is divisible by 60 frames.

Bass is hard to hear with small speakers.

But when I adjust the volume accordingly, the earphones are hard this time.

Square waves and sawtooth waves stand out even in the bass, but my ears hurt ..

entries.description:

Was just one day just thinking to myself "Hmmmm... what if Powell had actual percussion," and that's how this came to be. Really love this song a lot, despite not having played Trials of Mana (yet) and mostly hearing this game's fantastic OST in a bunch of hacks, back when Trials of Mana wasn't even an official name yet.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Flame Stag's Stage from Mega Man X2. Needed to clear my mind off some things, so I decided to do this song as a means of distracting myself from that.



It's one of my favorites from X2, despite its short length (and lackluster instrumentation). To be honest, I feel like Mega Man X2 has amazing compositions, but the instrumentation just feels very empty, especially when compared to X1 and many other really great SNES OSTs. Maybe it's because the channel usage in this one is limited or the samples used don't complement the songs really well, but most of these songs feel like they deserved better.



Important:

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of the Main BGM from China Warrior (aka The Kung Fu in Japan) for the TurboGrafx-16 / PC-Engine. Yeah, a game where you play as knock-off Bruce Lee and beat up some nuns has a banger OST (even though it's like 3 full songs and a couple jingles). Ended up playing this on my TurboGrafx-16 Mini back in December and fell in love with this theme.



I actually did start this port way back in April before getting too caught up on other songs. Luckily, I was able to get it finished now, and thank god I did. This song deserves some love, even if you don't ever plan on ever playing the game.



This is pretty lengthy song and also a great fit for auto-scrollers.

My first remix of my own composition (or I guess technically you can call this it's own composition, in which case, this is the fifth finished one).



After re-listening to Endless Nights I wondered if I can make it more boss battle themed and the result was this!



Some parts were from compositions that didn't go anywhere, like the intro, so I reused them, since they fit well here.



Was made to be used in boss battles, but I could also see its use in chase levels or intense castles with lasers.

Did an arrangement of Aya Shameimaru's theme from Touhou 9, Wind God Girl. It's a song that I've been meaning to do ever since I got into porting (like the many other songs I've said I wanted to do in the past lmao) and was one I was suggested quite often to do by many people. entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Quartz Quadrant JP from Sonic CD. Good freaking God is this song fantastic :DDDD. I stand by this (and every other time variation of the JP theme) being the best song in the entire game. Catchy melodies, fantastic instrumentation, a wonderful chord to support the song in the 2nd half, and that killer brass.



Sonic CD easily in my top 10 Sonic OSTs. It's a pure representation of 90s music, and I love it!!!



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. E / A Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. F / A# Minor (Past Pitch)

entries.description:
The mysterious yet singing theme from Rhythm Heaven Megamix's Songbird Remix, which is probably my favourite remix in the series. This song is quite a mish-mash, and even features some brief dubstep-y sections.



I ported this ages ago and showed it off during C3, but I was too lazy to loop it, as the original doesn't loop. Naturally, 3:00 a.m. on a school night is the best time to tackle MML surgery. I wasn't sure how best to loop it, as the song doesn't give many opportunities to do so, but hopefully you enjoy the point I picked.



Special thanks to Hazel for helping me play around with that noise pitchmod buildup thing.



Here's an image:
entries.name: Rhythm Heaven Megamix - Songbird Remix

Another banger too, 'cuz Mad Gear, unlike Metropolis, has some intense banging-ass tunes that fit the dark industrial stage incredibly well, especially this one, despite its short length. It's probs my favorite track from this game.

Did an arrangement of Yumeko's stage theme, The Last Judgement from Touhou 5: Mystic Square. Another Touhou 5 song under my belt, and it's another great song from an underappreciated OST!!!



It's a really great stage theme with an intensity that rivals that of Sakuya's stage theme from EoSD (though I do prefer this one over that one by a long shot, personally). It fits the pre-final stage very well and would've even been great as her boss theme if another stage theme was planned in mind.

Also known as "Intro" in another versions of The Lost Vikings.



A very funky, charming and upbeat theme played at the vikings village, and at the Heart Temple stage.



Somewhat big speechI've always loved listening to that song all day, and I ever wanted to port it someday. Of course, with the complexity of the game's OST, it proved to be a REALLY big challenge to port it, as the game's engine didn't want to do it justice. Though, I tried my best to port everything as accurately as I could, trying to replicate all of the GAIN's effects and pitches, and here it is.

entries.description:
𝐔𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐲𝐨𝐮, 𝐈 𝐝𝐨𝐧'𝐭 𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐝 𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠.



Did an arrangement of the theme that ushered a new era of Touhou, A Dream that is more Scarlet than Red from Touhou 6: Embodiment of the Scarlet Devil. Returning to doing Touhou title themes after a year, and I took a lot of heavy inspiration from the Touhou Luna Nights version.



It's a great song that introduced the famous lemotif that'd follow future game theme songs, and it's simple yet very iconic. Hell, I even used it in some of my Mega Man remixes, lmao.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End," Yoshi, P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. D# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. F Minor (MIDI Pitch)

3. E Minor (Custom Pitch)

entries.description:
This was a rather difficult one to get right, I managed to pull through, though.



This is the Blizzard Buffalo's Theme from Mega Man X3, my favorite song from the game.



It really fits well with the stage. Has that heavy snow feel to it, like you're powering through a massive blizzard and occasionally stopping to recover from the cold.



Fits in literally any snowy environment, and maybe even an ice factory of sorts. (Yes, they exist, look it up)



Oh, almost forgot, there is a toggle option in the .txt file that lets you change the lead between @0 (flute) and @13 (harp).

entries.description:

entries.description:
Decided to make my 200th port upload on this site something special similar to my Air Man Remix in February, so I did a special remix of SMWC's National Anthem Underworld Forest from Last Bible III.



History Of The SMWC National AnthemSix years ago, legendary porter Nanako made a port of this song, and little did anyone know that it'd change the entire Super Mario World industry. Nearly every SMW hack had this theme in it in some way or form. You could not escape it, even if you tried. And to make things worse, a year ago, other legendary porter Samantha made an unsampled port to add to the chaos. SMWCentral has never been the same since. What was once an innocent web site for gamers who wanted to express their love for the amazing Super Mario World has now turned into an Underworld Forest cult. SMWCentral deprived themselves of their Super Mario World content in order to please the Underworld Forest god with using this song in their hacks. This site is stuck in an endless cycle of torture of making sure this song was engraved into our brains, note for note, and us porters are forced to port / arrange this song or else our end will come. This is not just an end of an era. but it's the true end of... The Time-when-Underworld-Forest-wasn't-a-thing Days...



Jokes aside though, this song's absolutely fantastic (and so are those ports). There's a reason why so many people love using it, and I hope I was able to spice things up with my take on this awesome theme for my special! :D



Important:

♠ "Bonus End," & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. B Minor w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch, Listening-Only)

2. B Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)

2. C Minor (Original Pitch)

2. A# Minor (Custom Pitch)

The somberish fourth photo theme from the 9.5th Touhou game, Shoot the Bullet.

entries.description:
Ever wondered what the music would sound like if Mario is Missing! for the NES was ever expanded upon?

Well, I certainly was and the result was this!



It's a pretty neato composition I'd say, it captures some stuff from the original and turns it into something new.

The percussion is a bit of unhinged compered to how it is in the actual game, but I think it has a certain charm to it that compliments the song well.



Will I end up doing more?

Certainly, but not actively, maybe once a couple months.



Anyway, this song can be used in retro levels and cities.

It can be a bit repetitive after a while, so keep that in mind!

entries.description:
Merry Christmas!.. I guess...



This rather peculiar track plays in the Unlicensed NES game, Little Red Hood.



As far as I know (+ Zophar telling me) this is the only song that plays in the game, yup, nothing else, just this the whole game.

The game itself is known to be very cryptic and sometimes downright unplayable, almost everything is basically random.



I wont go into too much detail, but if you are interested, check it out somewhere on the internet. (AVGN made a video on it as well)



That's it, I guess, happy holidays!

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝 𝐈 𝐍𝐎𝐓 𝐞𝐱𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐢𝐭?



Did an arrangement of Hakurei ~ Eastern Wind from Touhou 2: Story Of Eastern Wonderland for Super Famicompo 3. The song that essentially started it all... the hell of bullets in Gensokyo... and I felt the need to do it for this contest. Really wanted to try basing it off both the original PC-98 and SC-88 MIDI versions given how vastly different both are while still tryna maintain my style (which was probably successful given the ... guesses of who did this song in the SFC3 results' guesses).



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.
entries.name: Touhou Fuumaroku ~ the Story Of Eastern Wonderland - Return Of The Gohei ~ Hakurei ~ Eastern Wind (Remix)

entries.description:
Did a Mega Man Stage Select Medley arrangement for the Super Famicompo 3. Honest to God, I've wanted to do this port for a long time now, especially after one of my friends gave me the idea to do it. It was probably the song that took me the longest out of my four entries for this contest. Really happy to have done this for it and also super happy lotsa people liked it to the point it even got 6th place!!! :DDD



Would've tried to include the X series stage select themes too, but they're vastly different than their classic counterparts. Maybe an X series stage select medley in the future?



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. F Minor (Remix Pitch, turned on default)

2. E Minor (Custom Pitch)

entries.description:
MERRY CHRISTMAS! The bonus final boss theme of R-ACK's v10.0.0. update, which is a "Mega Man X Styled" version of God Badorrer's theme from Brandish 2. Good as a general boss theme or even final bosses if you're looking for something a lot more exciting.



Setting LOOP2 to 1 will enable Zero's theme to "siivagunner" the original melody every second loop. Otherwise, the actual length is 1:09 and will take up 0x0909 bytes with staccato enabled (0x0985 bytes with staccato disabled).



Size of the song on this download page is based on the defines that cause the most space (LOOP2 enabled, Staccato disabled). Size of samples is 0x5DD7 bytes if they aren't already in the game.

entries.description:
The stage 1 theme from マリオ永草億　～ Illusionary Blossom of Cranium Prayer.



A happy and cheery, summery stage 1 song that sends you off on an adventure. I think of a lovely blue sky with a lush green landscape below it.

entries.description:
The stage 2 theme from マリオ永草億　～ Illusionary Blossom of Cranium Prayer.



It's a song that alternates between two different sections, hence the name. Since the lead starts with @5, I tried to make the intro section sound a bit like an old port from 2009, after which the rest of the song comes in full blast.

entries.description:

entries.description:
The goal theme from マリオ永草億　～ Illusionary Blossom of Cranium Prayer.

Note that, with the default SMW goal, the song will cut out abruptly at the end once the iris animation starts. It's not disruptive or anything, but still worth noting.

entries.description:
The player's score theme from マリオ永草億　～ Illusionary Blossom of Cranium Prayer.



...except it's not actually in the original hackjam entry. I decided to make this song after the fact, for fun. Just as the normal Touhou player's score theme is an arrangement of Kanako's theme, I decided to make this one an arrangement of Signal Vibrancy ~ Rhodochrose Illusion.



Includes an option to disable the fade-in by changing a define.

entries.description:
What a title, huh? (Yes, it's a Mother 3 reference.) Super Mario Maker's SMB Ghost House theme is a song I do enjoy listening to, so I decided "hey what the heck I'll remix it". I'll give myself credit, I think I made it sound a lot darker! This would actually fit a dungeon more, but if you enable percussion it can even sound factory-like.



There's 4 versions you can set in the "EnablePercussion" define:

- Default. (just the ghost house theme, no bells and whistles) Length is 1:23, Size is 0x0214.

- Enable Percussion on second loop. Length is 2:46, Size is 0x0350.

- Enable Percussion on second loop and loop percussion. Length is 2:05, Size is 0x028F.

- Start with Percussion and loop it. Length is 1:23, Size is 0x028F.



Nothing else to note, song is compatible with all sfx and global songs. It also only adds the percussion samples if you enable them, otherwise it'll stick to just the 4 main samples.
entries.name: Super Mario Maker - The House Mario Ignored Is A Dungeon?! ~ SMB Ghost House

It has been showcase at C3 Winter 2022.

entries.description:

Fun Fact: This was supposed to be for C3 Summer 2021, but because of a bunch of other songs I felt more inclined to do, I scrapped this and brought it back alive for this C3.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.
entries.name: Mega Man Battle Network 4 - Jack into Battle!! ~ Virus Busting (Remix)

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Dracula's Tears from Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow for C3 Winter 2021. One of the most underappreciated songs in the entire series and one of my favorite Castlevania themes as well. It's so freaking awesome!!!



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.
entries.name: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow - Sins of Science ~ Dracula's Tears (Remix)

entries.description:
𝗜 𝗰𝗮𝗻'𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝘀𝘁𝘂𝗽𝗶𝗱 𝘆𝗼𝘂... 𝗲𝗿, 𝗜 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻, 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗹𝘂𝗰𝗸.



Did an arrangement of Swanky's Swing / Bonus Intro from the game of God for C3 Winter 2022. So glad I've finally done a song from this game. It just means so freaking much to me as a video game and as a relic of my childhood!!! Even for a song that has quite a short loop, it's so freaking good, just like the rest of this... masterpiece of a soundtrack from our lord and savior, David freaking Wise!!!



How long did it take for you to realize that the Bonus Intro theme had the rest of the song from Swanky's Swing?



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. C# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. D Minor (Custom Pitch)
entries.name: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest - Spotlight on Kong ~ Swanky's Swing / Bonus Intro (Remix)

entries.description:

Did an arrangement of Stand Proud from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3 for C3 Winter 2021. Did this one for a friend and really wanted to hammer in an OP theme once again. Did Chase and Bloody Stream before, and it'd be wrong if I didn't do the one from the most memed Jojo part.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. A Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Underwater City from Rudra no Hihou (Treasure of the Rudras in English). Thought it'd be fun to do my own take on another Squ'enix theme, though I have not gotten the chance to play this game yet. Mostly heard this OST from other hacks and from listening to the soundtrack on my own time in the past.



Regardless, absolutely amazing theme!! Has a very ancient yet magical vibe that Square was definitely known for doing with a lot of their traditional RPG OSTs at the time.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

4. C Minor (Custom Pitch)

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of the only song from Super Mario Kart with good instrumentation, Vanilla Lake (Final Version). Given it's been a hot minute since I last did a Mario Kart track, and I thought I'd do another one of my favorite tracks in the series and turn that into a dance mix similar to a couple of my other songs of the past.



One of the best songs in the entire series, if you ask me, and it's one of the only good ones that came out of the mess that is SMK's OST. Listen, I ain't gonna bash on the songs themselves as they're mostly awesome, but the instrumentation is like if someone made their first ever midi and decided to only use what samples sounded the coolest rather than what works with the song.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled (for both versions).



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. E Major w/ slight detune (Remix Pitch - Listening-Only [SFX with be detuned if used in-game])

2. E Major (Original Pitch, turned on default)

4. D# Major (Custom Pitch 2)

entries.description:
Othello World is one of those Othello games you probably saw in some Japanese pawn shop or something like that. Developed by Dice and published by Tsukuda Original, it's very obscure, though easier to find at your nearest online shop for pretty cheap. Surprisingly, according to GDRI, it uses HAL's N-SPC variant, which is also used in games such as Kirby Super Star. In fact, every HAL game uses this sound driver, with the exception of EarthBound, which instead uses another N-SPC variant.



This jingle plays upon finishing a stage. After that, we get the counter and another jingle plays (varies if you either lost or win).



Good for goals, if it wasn't that obvious. There's even a flag in the TXT file that allows you to add the goal whistle at the start of the song.



This is the sampled version.
entries.name: Othello World - End of Game

A nice water-y or ruins song with some big stakes involved.

-------------

Important update:



On the former version, it was brought to my attention by Stivi, that calling Pause was not interrupting the song, but rather letting it freeze in place on the last played note.



It occurs on AddMusicK1.0.8 when channel #6, which plays the pause SFX, has noise inside, as explained by KungFuFurby and Kevin.



While I could have chosen to take #6's contents to channel #7, I found this choice inesthetical since #7 always gets cut with Jump or coin sounds. So I just replaced the noise sample of #6 by an external closed hat sample.

Back at it again with the Ys III remixes after a year of not doing one, and it's A Searing Struggle this time. Heavily based off the Genesis version's "Burning Fight" / PC-88 Version and the PC-Engine CD Version. Similar to the other songs in this OST, this song's SNES version got pretty duped when ported, though I will say the orchestral hit does actually give this version a bit of its own flair. Easily another highlight in this fantastic soundtrack, especially the Genesis, PC-Engine, and Oath in Felghana versions, which are just... way too amazing!!!

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of The Demon Underworld from Alcahest. Seriously, for an obscure (but really awesome) Super-Famicom-Only Action RPG by HAL, Jun Ishikawa went hard on this OST. This soundtrack feels like a blend of Ishikawa's style in Kirby Super Star with Nobuo Uematsu's style in the SNES Final Fantasy games. It's easily my favorite Kirby soundtrack given its style and the compositions here.



Originally was planning on doing Panakeian Castle, but I thought I'd give a spotlight to the heavily underrated endgame stage theme 'cuz it's amazing. What's with Squaresoft games having amazing endgame themes anyways?

entries.description:
One day every person in this nation will control their OWN destiny. A land of the truly free, dammit. A nation of action, not words. Ruled by strength, not committee.



Did an arrangement of the Senator Armstrong's last phase theme, It Has To Be this Way (aka "Standing Here") from Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, despite it not being as long as the original (due to ARAM constrictions). Just got into the Metal Gear series recently (beating this game and MGS1), & MGR lives up to the hype of being one of the best action games ever made. Not only that, but it has one of the most kick-ass final boss themes in any action game period. I felt the need to do this theme given this game has no representation on this site (and really needs it), and it's become one of my favorite final boss themes now.



PS: This song is not actually used in the scene where Raiden punches Armstrong, despite memes telling you otherwise.

entries.description:
Lyrics:

Go Into The Nightmare!

Go Into The (Go Into The)

Go Into The Nightmare!

... Let's Go!

Go Into The Nightmare!

Go Into The, Go Into The,

Go Into The Nightmare!

... Let's Go!



(Vocalist is me, Daizo)



The incredibly rocked out boss theme used in the 4th Place WLDC2022 Entry "Fury of the Storm" where you fight Sir Kris Flurry (thank you ChaseNScooter for naming her and yes, she's a her.) As you might be able to tell, it's a song with vocal samples.



"CORRECTNESS" define will change the timing the sample "Let's Go!" is played. 0 is accurate to the contest entry, any other number plays it at it's proper timing.



Song is not compatible with Yoshi, P-switches, Bonus End, Contact/Clap, Thunder, and Blarggs, and Death. Would recommend Retry patch to get around the lack of a death theme. Contact/Clap is at least replaced with the snare included with the song so it still 'sounds' impactful instead of glitched.



PLEASE credit me. I don't sing too often, and I also composed the song itself so I'd very much appreciate the recognition.
entries.name: Fury of the Storm - Go Into The Nightmare

entries.description:
One of the first midi songs, bundled in Windows 98.

Happy-go-lucky song that starts quiet and goes wilder in the end,



good for credits or intro.



As the samples take up a lot of space, I've done a light version, to get it just change the following to 0:

Code; _______________switch to 0 for lower res___________
#define "hi_res" 1
; ________________________________________________



You can also add more delay by adding a rest to all channels.



Made on request for NopeContest



Major edit: As warned by brickblock369, I had got a channel completely wrong due to a midi misread, it is now fixed.

entries.description:
My Very Special 200th Submission!



This is objectively the best song in Undertale and no one can tell me otherwise.

The energy of this song perfectly depicts what happens in the game at this moment; It really makes you feel like you're fighting against a true hero of the story.



That being said, thank you so much for the support!

This originally started as me trying to port a single song from an unknown NES game and turned into something not even I can fully comprehend.

Anyway, enough rambling, Seg loves you all! See ya soon with more ports!



Oh yeah, I forgot to mention, it's not compatible with the Thunder SFX, blame the M&B Open Hat.

entries.description:
*A S C E N D S*





Did an arrangement of The Moon stage theme from DuckTales. What can I even say about this track that hasn't been said before. It's easily Disney's most iconic theme they had in any video game of theirs renditions of musicial numbers from the movies don't count. It's been arranged so much to the point where goddamn Jake Kaufman had to cough up a banger arrangement for the remake. It's one of my favorite songs on the NES, especially from a game I generally enjoyed when I was younger.

Did an arrangement of Keine Kamishirasawa's theme Nostalgic Blood of the East ~ Old World from Touhou 8: Imperishable Night. Probably the one Touhou theme I associate the most with SMW romhacking. It was one of the first Touhou songs I ever heard and fell in love with (alongside Keine's boss theme, Plain Asia). It's easily one of my favorite songs in the series for nostalgia alone, and it sucks that it's also one of the most criminally underrated theme in the series because it's so damn good!!! It's easily one of ZUN's best works, if you ask me.

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Jewel Temptation from Mega Man 9 for Summer C3 2022. Was feeling some RRThiel inspiration after listening to some songs on a couple car drives. I wanted to do something more funky for my next classic Mega Man remix. I don't do enough funky stuff, and I thought this would be a great time to start.



Jewel Man's stage theme is just another really good song. I really can't say much here that I haven't already said for the rest of this soundtrack. It's upbeat and very fitting for a underground "crystal caverns" stage.





Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. E Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. D# Minor (Custom Pitch)



There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. Enables Voice Clip, but disables Thunder, P-Switch, & Yoshi (turned on default)

2. Disables Voice Clip

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Infinity Mijinion's Stage theme from Mega Man X6 for Summer C3 2022. I originally did start this two months back but never got to finishing it (due to being unsatisfied with it). Luckily, I pushed through for this C3 and decided to give it the attention it deserves once again.



As a fan of The Final Countdown, Infinity Mijinion's stage theme is easily one of my favorite songs in the entire Mega Man franchise. I had to arrange this song for C3.



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. F# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

2. G Minor (Custom Pitch)



There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. Enables Voice Clip, but disables Thunder & P-Switch (turned on default)

2. Disables Voice Clip
entries.name: Mega Man X6 - Infinite Possibilities ~ Infinity Mijinion (Remix)

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Straight Ahead from Mega Man Zero 4 for Summer C3 2022. Been a while since I did another Mega Man Zero track. Zero 4 is my favorite of the Zero series (not counting ZX) and it easily has some of my favorite songs in the series too. I thought I'd take some more RRThiel inspiration for this one once again.



Straight Ahead's always been an interesting song to me mostly 'cuz it always reminded me of Sigma Stage 1 from Mega Man X.





Important:

♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. D# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of City from The Ninja Warriors for Summer C3 2022. I've been addicted to this soundtrack for the past couple months 'cuz it's filled with nothing but bangers. I've already done Best Room in the past (name fits the song), but I gotta give some love to stage 5's City theme. It's upbeat, deep, and it gets you pumped.



This game needs some more love. It has amazing music throughout the entire game, and the gameplay is awesome, even if it is also very challenging!



Important:

There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

entries.description:
My mortal enemy, Chang'e. Are you watching?!

Gaze upon this poor soul as she struggles between life and death!



Did an arrangement of Pure Furies ~ Whereabouts of the Heart from Touhou 15: Legacy of the Lunatic Kingdom for Summer C3 2022. This is probs the one song some of my mutuals has been waiting for ever since I showed off a WIP on Twitter dot com. I've been meaning to do Junko's theme ever since I did Junko's stage theme a year back. It also is the hardest and, arguably, the most ambitious port I've done so far ones. I had to really limit myself here in terms of sample usage, which kinda sucked, but I really think it paid off in the end.



Junko's theme is easily one of my favorite final boss themes in this series. It's hella intense and perfectly symbolizes her character as a rageful spirit who lost her son and wants to enact revenge on those who were responsible for his death (Chang'e and her husband).



Important:

♠ "Bonus End" is disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. C# Minor w/ slight detune (Remix - Listening-Only)

2. C# Minor (Original Pitch, turned on default)

3. C Minor (Custom Pitch)



There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

1. Enables Voice Clip, but disables Thunder, P-Switch, & Yoshi (turned on default)

2. Disables Voice Clip
entries.name: Touhou Kanjuden ~ Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom - Mother's Tormented Soul ~ Pure Furies ~ Whereabouts of the Heart (Remix)

It's a happy-sounding song, and feels magical just like a little fairy flying around, shooting bullets would.

But, why transcribe everything from scratch when I can just rip the note data from the almost-identical-save-for-a-few-grace-notes version from the Mario Kart DS prototype? It's actually different from the final MKDS version too!

One loop of the song actually contains the whole song twice but with the addition of a harp, and absence of a couple of hihats.



Thank you VecchiaZim and Masterlink for helping me transcribe and fiddle around with the almost inaudible harp sections of the original.

entries.description:
Did another Mega Man 4: Voyage arrangement, and it's Dive Man's Stage theme this time. Was replaying this hack recently, got to Dive Man's stage theme, and couldn't stop jamming for some time, almost forgetting how awesome his theme in this hack was. It's such a simple theme but so damn catchy. I thought it'd be another fun Mega Man romhack track to do.

entries.description:
The theme used in the level "Life has it's Ups and Downs" from Rakugaki Mario. This is a downported version of "real final" from R-ACK, which that song can be downloaded here. Not to be confused with the unsampled version. This can work for airships, castles, water levels, title screens, cutscenes, or even space levels.



This is specifically designed to emulate the same style as those older japanese ports from back then, which itself has a nostalgic feel for a lot of the older SMW hacking folk, me included. Of course, this "style" is not exclusive to japanese ports (a lot of older FPI and S.N.N. ports have that same feel), which is why it's more accurate to call it a "classic remix".

entries.description:
Adol Christin's first theme song in Ys I, composed by Yuzo Koshiro. This music is originally unused in the game, but it was later arranged by Ryo Yonemitsu to be repurposed as an intro cutscene theme for Hudson-developed TurboGrafx-CD version, Ys Book I & II. This song didn't return in the remake, Ys I & II Chronicles.



This port is likewise an amalgamation of the PC-8801 version and the arranged TurboGrafx-CD version. The general composition is based on the PC88 version (and thus doesn't include the extended guitar solo added by Yonemitsu), and some extra parts and instrument choices are based on the TGCD version.



This port uses the optimized SMW sample set.

Did an arrangement of The Concealed Four Seasons from Touhou 16. I've attempted to arrange this song a total of four times with this fourth one finally being a successful one to me. Took me nearly three weeks.



It's one of my favorite final boss themes in the series. The intensity, the pacing, the melodies, EVERYTHING ABOUT THIS SONG KICKS ASS!!! For a game with a pretty... by-the-numbers soundtrack (for Touhou standards), ZUN didn't have to put all his energy into this song, but HE DID (and that's what matters)!!!

𝒟𝑜 𝓎𝑜𝓊 𝓇𝑒𝒶𝓁𝓁𝓎 𝓊𝓃𝒹𝑒𝓇𝓈𝓉𝒶𝓃𝒹 𝓉𝒽𝒶𝓉?



Did an arrangement of Necrofantasia from Touhou 7: Perfect Cherry Blossom. Wanted to go for something a bit more "softer" than the original, though it makes this version of the song more unfitting for boss fights (might wanna go with the other Necrofantasia ports if that's what you originally wanted to use this song for).



I'm gonna be honest, I've never been a fan of Touhou 7's soundtrack, and I've also never been a fan of the original version of Necrofantasia. The original song's instrumentation to me always felt too chaotic for its own good, and I do understand that's part of the reason why most love it. But there are some really great arrangements of this song I've heard in not only some of the other games (primarily Touhou 15.5) but also some on YouTube, which heavily inspired me to do my own take on this. Plus, Yukari Yakumo's one of my favorite characters in the series, so I basically had to dedicate this to her. :P

entries.description:
A lovely song requested by Christina Hendricks, which plays in the area where you go to purify your Pokémon. Good for peaceful areas and overworlds.



The instrumental samples are from Kirby's Dream Land 3 (as requested), and the bird samples come from Fire Emblem: Genealogy of the Holy War.



OPTIONS: There are a few options available to toggle the music and bird noises.

 OPTION 0 - Song plays without bird sounds.

 OPTION 1 - Song plays with bird sounds.

 OPTION 2 - Only the bird sounds play (thanks to Dappertron for the idea!)



(This song holds a lot of nostalgia for me as someone who grew up playing XD: Gale of Darkness on the GameCube, and even though I didn't remember the exact song growing up, the area always left an impression on me for it's innate ability to instill a sense of calmness in the player.)

entries.description:
Although not as famous as chiptune Korobeiniki aka Type-A from the GameBoy version, it's a classic on its own right.



This track is a chiptune remix by Hirozaku Tanaka of Dance of the Suger Plum Fairy by Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky from the theatre performance The Nutcracker.

This specific port is in chiptune style and only makes use of four channels with hardcoded and simple instruments.



Best used for night time fun locations (e.g. a carnival or circus), puzzle levels and switch palaces.



Just be wary of giant vitamin pills dropping on top of you if you take too long.

entries.description:

entries.description:
My original submission for Super Famicompo 4, which won 3rd place.



The song tells of a nostalgic place, where many a memory was made in days before; yet it is but a memory, and all that remains of this place is a shell of what it once represented, usurped by time. Tangible as these might be, those old walls can never truly be revisited. I think we all have these kinds of places, and will accumulate more as time goes on, so this song serves as a celebration of those places and the feelings and memories we cherish from them.

entries.description:
𝕐𝕠𝕦 𝕤𝕔𝕣𝕒𝕞𝕓𝕝𝕖𝕕 𝕞𝕪 𝕖𝕝𝕖𝕔𝕥𝕣𝕠𝕟𝕤!



Did an arrangement of Fuse Man's Stage Theme ⚡ from Mega Man 11 for my 𝟒𝐊 𝐬𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐧𝐞. I hosted a tournament this time around for deciding on which Robot Master's theme was gonna get a special arrangement this time, and Fuse Man won the entire thing (against 15 other contestants) beating Snake Man in the last round.



Easily my favorite Robot Master stage theme in Mega Man 11. I always thought this track had the perfect intensity and pacing for a "Fuse Factory" stage. It's incredibly catchy and understandable why Fuse Man won the tournament. Also surprisingly works well with Desire Drive from Touhou 13. :P



Important:

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End" & Thunder SFX are disabled.



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. D Minor (Original Pitch) [turned on by default]

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. D# Minor (Custom Pitch 1)

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. C# Minor (Custom Pitch 2)



There are also customizable versions for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ1. Enables Voice Clip, but at the cost of SMW-Compatibility

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ2. Disables Voice Clip [turned on default]

[2022/02/15] Update: Made the echo less horrible.

entries.description:
The "stage 6" theme from the game-without-a-game, PC-98 Touhou-style music album, 東方奇界泉　～ Adventures in Inferno. Like a lot of stage 6 themes in the official games, this one is short, and ramps up in intensity before calming back down as the boss would show up. In that regard, it's probably good for tense, final areas.



Update: Fixed an octave inaccuracy and filled in the percussion at the beginning, thank you brickblock369!



[2022/02/15] Update: Fixed more octave inaccuracies and tweaked some instruments.
entries.name: Touhou Kikaisen ~ Adventures in Inferno - Going Down the Road to Yomi

entries.description:
A happy, cheery song from Twinkle Star Sprites. I've never played this game but I absolutely adore this song. It could best fit energetic levels, probably sky ones as the name implies.



[2022/02/15] Update: Ported the song from scratch for better accuracy and mixing! It's also light-sampled now as a result, with the funniest sample probably being a higher @5 for literally one note that would otherwise overflow.
entries.name: Twinkle Star Sprites (Neo Geo) - Love Me (Sky Stage 1)

entries.description:
The energetic, life-is-good Past music from Stardust Speedway, and one of my favourite Past songs. Probably best known for its iconic HUEHUEHUEHUE sample, which is also in this port, in its uncompressed glory. Fitting for happy and comfortable night stages.



[2022/02/15] Update: Reported from scratch for better mixing, instrumentation that makes more sense, and pitchmod that's done with intention.
entries.name: Sonic CD - Stardust Speedway Zone (Past)

entries.description:
A song that's fairly energetic despite its name, probably best known as the title screen music from Lyle in Cube Sector. Likely fits title screens or other such areas.



Includes two versions for the lead, one using @6, and one using @2, the latter being inspired by neodym65's Superfamicompo 4 port of the same song.

entries.description:
The title screen theme from 東方魔宝城 ～ Book of Star Mythology, a pretty well-known Touhou fangame with lots of stars in it, and a bizarre take on LoLK's Pointdevice Mode which just lets you die as much as you want with no penalty. As a Touhou title screen theme, it has the Theme of Eastern Story leitmotif in it, albeit very subtly.



Fitting with the theme of the game, it's pretty sparkly and dreamy-sounding.



Also, I don't think Asterhyshm is a word.
entries.name: Touhou Mahoujou ~ Book of Star Mythology - Fantastic Tale of One Night ~ Asterhyshm Line

entries.description:
This is an original song (well... essentially it is, but sampling-wise not so much since it uses the Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Pasts's Mirror song as a sample, though naturally with plenty of downsampling to avoid memory constraints, and also in this particular case to give some breathing room and a bit of a lo-fi-esque atmosphere due to the quality reduction that occurs) created for the realms of the bizarre and unusual. Although I technically created it as a overworld theme (going by the tag I gave it as well as the track name), musically I let it drift on for a little while longer, meaning technically it can also work as a semi-background-esque level theme.



Contains two user defines: one is a master echo enable switch, and the other one enables it for the music. Echo for SFX, within the context of AddmusicK 1.0.8, the latest moderated version at the time of this release, (which still requires the master echo enable switch to be on) is handled through 1DFA commands $05 and $06: use 1DFA command $06 right after the song starts to enable echo for SFX.

Gets a bit repetitive.

entries.description:
Demon, death is too good for you! 🦇



Did an arrangement of Dracula's Castle from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night to celebrate the Return to Castlevania DLC for Dead Cells.



We all know how iconic it is! It's the first thing you hear once you enter Dracula's doors into his newest and most biggest castle (at the time). It's such an amazing theme song for the amazing game that changed the world forever!!!



Hooded's Obsessive Shilling Over Dead Cells & Why You Should Play ItDead Cells is a must-play for any Castlevania, Metroidvania, and Rogue-lite fans. It's an underrated masterpiece that continues to be a better live-service than every live-service game out there (w/o even being a real live-service game in the first-place) w/ constant updates adding new content to the already-finished game. Its combat is fluent, its level design is perfect, its atmosphere is tense and Castlevania-like, IT'S ALL PERFECT, AND YOU SHOULD PLAY IT!!!



SERIOUSLY! WHAT ARE YOU DOING WITH YOUR LIFE RIGHT NOW?!?! GO BUY IT!!! PLZ!!! IT'S SO FREAKING AMAZING!!!

entries.description:
My submission to 120hoSPC#10, which won 2nd place.



Per the rules of the contest, this song only uses one sample (@13). The tune itself is heavily remixed, with a sort of "1950's jazz" style to it. I would've liked to have captured more of the counter-melody that the original has going on, what with this being a song about two people and all, but I'm still content with how it came out.



I realized the song sounded good when I slowed it in the SPC player with pitch sync on, so I added a "Slowed & Reverb" toggle option.



(And no, the game has nothing to do with the Jesus you're thinking of, it's a spaceship :))

entries.description:
Did an arrangement of Robotnik Winter Zone Act 2 from Sonic Triple Trouble 16-Bit. I needed to get back on that Sonic grindset with another song, and with this remake being one of the best things I've played this year (so far), I thought I'd give it some love.



Robotnik Winter Zone ShillingRobotnik Winter Zone was already the best zone in the OG game, but they managed to make it the BESTEST zone in this game. Seriously, Act 2 had every right going as hard as it did, but it's just... AAAAAAAA!!! I love Act 1's rendition, but this is just the cherry on top of what is already the best cake Robotnik Winter Zone fans are eating!! THIS ZONE IS GODDAMN PEAK!!!



Perfect for stages where you're riding a snowboard while an avalanche chases you!

Important:

There's an option to enable or disable the SMW death SFX at the beginning:

ㅤ0. No Death SFX [turned on by default]

ㅤ1. Death SFX





Mod Note: If using this as a global song (such as the death or game over songs), you will need to add ! to the line featuring @14 in Addmusic_sample_groups.txt for it to sound as intended.



Update:

Added an option to change the sample in the song (for those who want to use it globally w/o any workarounds):

ㅤ1. @1 (Works globally by default) [turned on by default]

ㅤ2. @14

𝒪𝓊𝓇 𝑔𝓇𝓊𝒹𝑔𝑒 𝓌𝒾𝓁𝓁 𝒷𝑒 𝓈𝑒𝓉𝓉𝓁𝑒𝒹 𝒶𝓉 𝓁𝒶𝓈𝓉...

Did an arrangement of the one and only, Masked Dedede's Theme, from Kirby Super Star Ultra for my 5K subscriber milestone. A massive goal reached deserves some treatment from the King himself. I already did his theme once... now it's time to do it again!!!



It shouldn't be a surprise when I say this is my favorite Kirby theme and one of my favorite final boss themes in any video game period. Seriously, to top the original song (which is already one of the best songs in the series) with this is an achievement very few can achieve.



Important:

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ "Bonus End," P-Switch, & Thunder SFX are disabled.

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ♠ Death sound is gonna sound weird (@1 replaces @9 to save on space).



There are also customizable pitches for this song that you can adjust in the song's txt file:

‎‎‎‎‎‎‎‎ㅤ3. C Minor (Original Pitch)

entries.description:
The Extra Stage theme from a Touhou-style music album by Chama.



It's a very repetitive song, with slight variations on one phrase that repeats over and over. Despite that, it feels very energetic.



Special thanks to icrawfish for helping me transcribe the piano chords I couldn't make out in the one unique section.
entries.name: Touhou Ensougetsu ~ Blue Moon Rhapsody - Crystal Shine Road

entries.description:
The "stage 2" theme from the game-without-a-game, PC-98 Touhou-style music album, 東方奇界泉　～ Adventures in Inferno.



It's energetic and reminiscent of Dimension of Rêverie from Mystic Square. The composition itself is chaotic, with lots of things going on at once during the fast parts. The port itself reminds me of old 2009 Touhou ports too! The magic of @5 and @14…
entries.name: Touhou Kikaisen ~ Adventures in Inferno - Hellish Dreams, Everlasting

entries.description:
The early stages theme from Touhou 16.5, Violet Detector. It's melancholic and uncertain-sounding, with a happyish resolution at the end.



I don't know what ZUN did while mixing this song but everything but the lead felt inaudible to me while transcribing, so y'know, liberties were potentially taken.
entries.name: Hifuu Nightmare Diary ~ Violet Detector - Lucid Dreamer
Breezy Disk '99

entries.description:
The theme of the lesser-known blue sphere-getting special stage from the Sonic series. Knuckles and friends run through Polyhedron Land collecting orbs in a stage that truly shows off the 32X's capabilities.



I had to sacrifice panning accuracy on those background @4s in favour of actually including both notes as a chord sample. The joys of 8 channels.
entries.name: Knuckles' Chaotix - Tube Panic

entries.description:
A tense and repetitive song from Knuckles' Chaotix. It starts a little chaotic, then gets a little tense.



I can't remember where this plays in the game, but I would presume some lategame cutscene.
entries.name: Knuckles' Chaotix - Pendulum

entries.description:
A remix of Bloody Tears, not from Castlevania II, but from WaiWai World 2!



I love Bloody Tears a lot, but I feel like most remixes of it don't do it justice because they make it dull and dreary. I find it works much better as an energetic song. So I slapped a bunch of piano and orchestra hits into it and here we are! And a solo for good measure.
entries.name: WaiWai World 2: SOS!! Parsley Jō - Bloody Tears (Remix)

entries.description:
A remix of Aquarius from Castlevania III.



I tried to follow the same spark I had after my remix of Bloody Tears. This one's pretty experimental, especially in the second loop.



Maybe it's the name of the song, but I tried to get for a very wet sound, whatever that means.
entries.name: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse  - Aquarius (Remix)

entries.description:
Metal Squad from TFIV, the track everyone loves to say could never be done on a SNES, is now done on the SNES and here for you to use in SMW hacks!!!!!!!!!!! Cool!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!



Anyway, with how rocking this track is, it's best suited for more intense kinds of levels, like a castle, lava, athletic, and maybe even a abstract/space stage if you're able to include some kinda shmup level thing somehow, I dunno; obviously though, where you use this is up to you really, so yeah, don't take this as a end-all-be-all or anything lmao



(oh yeah, and boss fights too I guess.)
entries.name: Thunder Force IV - Metal Squad

entries.description:
The song that plays for one of the Titan fights in Sonic Frontiers, A.K.A widely considered by many to be the hypest fuckin' thing in that game, and for damn good reason.



Anyway, for me at least, this seems to be best suited to boss and final boss fights almost exclusively, so I dunno whether or not it can fit in a level, but regardless I've added a looped and non-looped version to fit whatever needs you desire... well, technically you'll have to manually edit the .txt file for that to work (change the ? in the text file to / and vice-versa basically), but I just didn't want to clutter up the .zip file with too much shit this time around so uh, yeah.
